Infants only a few months old look longer at events that break the rules of solid objects, which suggests that they expect objects to persist and not to pass through one another. Children acquire grammar from a small and messy sample of speech, a fact Noam Chomsky called the poverty of the stimulus and took as proof of an inborn language faculty. And a question that the Irish scientist William Molyneux put to Locke in 1688 has been tested. Would a man born blind, who knew a cube and a sphere by touch, recognize them by sight alone if he were suddenly able to see? Locke said no. In 2011 researchers in India examined children just after surgery for congenital blindness. They could not match what they saw to what they felt, and they learned to do it within days.
paras.zh: 有三條研究路線改變了這場辯論。才幾個月大的嬰兒，對違反固體規則的事件注視得比較久；這顯示他們預期物體會持續存在，而且不會彼此穿透。孩子從少量而雜亂的語言樣本就習得了文法；喬姆斯基把這個事實稱為「刺激的貧乏」，並且當作天生語言機能的證明。還有，愛爾蘭科學家莫利紐茲在 1688 年向洛克提出的一個問題，已經被檢驗了。一個生來失明、靠觸覺認得立方體與球體的人，如果突然看得見，單憑視覺認得出它們嗎？洛克說不能。2011 年，研究者在印度檢查了剛做完先天性失明手術的孩子。他們沒辦法把看到的跟摸到的配對起來；而他們在幾天之內就學會了。

paras.en: That result is a fair picture of where things stand. The newly sighted children had no ready-made knowledge linking sight to touch, as Locke predicted. They acquired it far faster than blank paper could, as Leibniz would have predicted. Neither side has been proved simply right. What has faded is the old either-or.
paras.zh: 這個結果，相當公允地呈現了目前的局面。剛復明的孩子並沒有現成的、把視覺連到觸覺的知識，如洛克所預言。他們習得這種知識的速度，遠比白紙做得到的快，如萊布尼茲會預言的。沒有哪一邊被證明是單純地對。淡出的是舊日那個「非此即彼」。

essay.h_en: Why it matters to a teacher

paras.en: The question was never only academic. If the mind is white paper, education is everything, and differences among people are differences in what has been written on them. Locke drew that conclusion, and it has been a great engine of reform. If the mind has veins, a teacher’s task is to find them and work with them, which is what Socrates did in the sand. Each view has its danger. The first tempts us to think that children can be made into anything. The second tempts us to read our expectations into their nature. Mencius’s image may be the wisest of the three, since a sprout has a nature of its own and still has to be tended. He warns against the farmer who, impatient with his slow crop, went out and pulled on the shoots to help them grow.
paras.zh: 這個問題從來不只是學術的。如果心靈是白紙，教育就是一切，人與人的差別就是寫在他們身上的東西的差別。洛克得出了這個結論，而它一直是改革的強大引擎。如果心靈有紋路，老師的任務就是找出紋路、順著它們工作；蘇格拉底在沙地上做的正是這件事。兩種看法各有危險。第一種誘使我們以為孩子可以被塑造成任何樣子。第二種誘使我們把自己的期待讀進他們的本性裡。孟子的意象也許是三者當中最有智慧的，因為芽有它自己的本性，卻仍然需要照料。他警告我們別學那個農夫：嫌莊稼長得慢，就跑去把苗一棵棵往上拔。

lab.title_zh: 親手做一次：把正方形加倍
lab.lead_en: This is the problem Socrates set the boy, with the same wrong turnings. You will not be told the answer. Watch what the questions do, and decide afterward whether you were taught or reminded.
lab.lead_zh: 這是蘇格拉底出給少年的那道題，連走錯的路都一樣。沒有人會告訴你答案。留意這些問題做了什麼，然後再判斷：你是被教會的，還是被提醒的？

say.en: Here is a square whose side is 2 feet. Its area is 4 square feet. I want a square with twice the area, 8 square feet. How long must its side be?
say.zh: 這是一個邊長 2 尺的正方形，面積是 4 平方尺。我要一個面積兩倍、也就是 8 平方尺的正方形。它的邊長該是多少？

t.en: Twice as long: 4 feet
t.zh: 兩倍長：4 尺

t.en: 3 feet
t.zh: 3 尺

say.en: Let us draw it. A side of 4 gives this square. Count how many of the original squares fit inside it.
say.zh: 我們把它畫出來。邊長 4 得到這個正方形。數數看，裡面放得下幾個原來的正方形？

note.en: Four of them: 16 square feet. Doubling the side made the square four times as large. The boy gave this answer first, and Socrates remarks to Meno: “now he fancies that he knows.”
note.zh: 四個：16 平方尺。把邊長加倍，正方形變成四倍大。少年第一次就是這樣答的；蘇格拉底對美諾說：「現在他自以為知道。」

t.en: Then it must be between 2 and 4: 3 feet
t.zh: 那一定介於 2 和 4 之間：3 尺

say.en: A side of 3 gives this square. What is its area?
say.zh: 邊長 3 得到這個正方形。它的面積是多少？

note.en: Three times three is 9, and we wanted 8. This was the boy’s second answer. He now says: “Indeed, Socrates, I do not know.” Socrates remarks that he is better off than before, when he did not know and thought he did.
note.zh: 三乘三是 9，而我們要的是 8。這是少年的第二個答案。這時他說：「真的，蘇格拉底，我不知道。」蘇格拉底評論說，他比先前好多了；先前他不知道，卻以為自己知道。

t.en: I do not know. Show me another line.
t.zh: 我不知道。請再畫一條線給我看。

say.en: Take the large square again, made of four of the original. Now I draw a line from corner to corner across each of the four. Each line cuts its square in half. How many halves lie inside the tilted figure?
say.zh: 再看那個由四個原正方形拼成的大正方形。現在我在四個正方形裡各畫一條對角線。每條線把它所在的正方形切成兩半。斜著的那個圖形裡面，有幾個「半個」？

t.en: Two
t.zh: 兩個

t.en: Four
t.zh: 四個

t.en: Eight
t.zh: 八個

say.en: Four halves, each of 2 square feet, make 8. So the square built on the diagonal is double the original. Its side is the diagonal of the first square, a length that cannot be written as any whole number or fraction of feet.
say.zh: 四個「半個」，每個 2 平方尺，合起來是 8。所以在對角線上作出的正方形，是原來的兩倍。它的邊就是第一個正方形的對角線；這個長度，寫不成任何整數尺或分數尺。

note.en: Socrates: “Without any one teaching him he will recover his knowledge for himself, if he is only asked questions.” Plato concludes that the boy is recollecting. A skeptic replies that the questions were leading ones and the drawing did the teaching. What nobody disputes is that the boy now sees why the answer must be true, and that this is something no amount of measuring could have shown him.
note.zh: 蘇格拉底說：「沒有任何人教他，只要有人問他問題，他就會自己把知識找回來。」柏拉圖的結論是，少年在回憶。懷疑的人回答說，那些都是誘導性的問題，真正在教的是那張圖。沒有人爭論的是：少年現在看出了答案為什麼「必定」為真，而這是量再多次也量不出來的。

q.en: Molyneux’s question (1688): a man born blind knows a cube and a sphere by touch. He is made to see. Before touching them, can he tell by sight which is which?
q.zh: 莫利紐茲的問題（1688）：一個生來失明的人，靠觸覺認得立方體與球體。現在他被治好、看得見了。在碰到它們之前，他能單憑視覺分辨哪個是哪個嗎？

yes.en: Leibniz said yes, given time to reason: a sphere has no corners and a cube has eight, and that structure is the same for sight and touch.
yes.zh: 萊布尼茲說能，只要給他時間推理：球沒有角，立方體有八個角，而這個結構對視覺與觸覺是相同的。

no.en: Locke and Molyneux said no: he has not yet learned which look goes with which feel.
no.zh: 洛克與莫利紐茲說不能：他還沒學到哪一種樣子對應哪一種觸感。

result.en: The test was finally run in 2011, on children in India who had just had surgery for congenital blindness. They could not match the seen object to the felt one, performing near chance. Within about a week they could. The connection is learned, as Locke said, and learned remarkably fast, which suggests that the mind was prepared for it.
result.zh: 這個測驗終於在 2011 年做了，對象是印度一群剛做完先天性失明手術的孩子。他們沒辦法把看到的物體跟摸到的配起來，答對率接近亂猜。大約一週之內，他們就做得到了。這個連結是學來的，如洛克所說；而且學得驚人地快，這顯示心靈早就為此做好了準備。

argument.lead_en: Locke opens the Essay by trying to clear innate ideas out of the way. His argument is short, and Leibniz’s reply to it set the terms of the debate. Click a step to see what can be said against it.
argument.lead_zh: 洛克在《人類理解論》一開頭，就想把天生觀念清出場。他的論證很短，而萊布尼茲對它的回應，定下了這場辯論的格局。點任何一步，看看別人可以怎麼反對它。

steps.en: If a principle were innate, it would be present in every human mind from the beginning.
steps.zh: 如果某個原則是天生的，它就會從一開始就存在於每一個人的心靈裡。
steps.ob_en: Accepted by both sides, as long as “present” is left undefined. Everything turns on what it means for something to be in a mind.
steps.ob_zh: 只要不去界定「存在」，雙方都接受。一切都取決於：一樣東西「在心靈裡」是什麼意思。

steps.en: Nothing can be in the mind without the mind’s being aware of it. To say a notion is imprinted and yet unnoticed “is to make this impression nothing.”
steps.zh: 沒有任何東西可以在心靈裡，而心靈卻沒有察覺到它。說一個概念被印上了、卻沒被注意到，「等於把這個印記說成什麼都不是」。
steps.ob_en: This is the step most often attacked. Leibniz answered that the mind holds a great deal it is not attending to: memories, habits, and skills such as one’s grasp of grammar. Innate knowledge is like these, a disposition waiting for the occasion. Modern psychology is on his side, since most of what the mind does is not conscious.
steps.ob_zh: 這是最常被攻擊的一步。萊布尼茲回答說，心靈裡有大量它並沒有在注意的東西：記憶、習慣，以及像掌握文法這樣的技能。天生知識就像這些，是一種等待機緣的傾向。現代心理學站在他這邊，因為心靈做的事，大部分都不是有意識的。

steps.en: Young children and many adults are not aware of even the most basic principles, such as “it is impossible for the same thing to be and not to be.”
steps.zh: 幼兒與許多成年人，連最基本的原則都沒有察覺到，例如「同一樣東西不可能既是又不是」。
steps.ob_en: True of the principle stated in words. But a child who is astonished when an object vanishes is relying on something like it. Using a principle and being able to state it are different achievements.
steps.ob_zh: 就這個原則的「文字表述」而言，這是真的。可是，一個看到東西憑空消失而大吃一驚的孩子，倚賴的正是某種類似的東西。運用一個原則，跟說得出這個原則，是兩種不同的成就。

steps.en: Therefore no principles are innate.
steps.zh: 所以，沒有任何原則是天生的。
steps.ob_en: The conclusion follows only for innate knowledge of the conscious kind, which few of Locke’s opponents had defended. Against dispositions and built-in capacities the argument has no force, and Locke himself assumes that the mind is born with powers of comparing, combining, and abstracting.
steps.ob_zh: 這個結論只對「有意識的」那種天生知識成立，而洛克的對手很少有人為那種知識辯護過。對於傾向與內建的能力，這個論證毫無力量；而洛克自己也預設，心靈生來就有比較、組合、抽象的能力。

source.work: John Locke, An Essay Concerning Human Understanding (1690); Plato, Meno
source.work_zh: 洛克《人類理解論》；柏拉圖《美諾篇》
source.tr: Locke in the original English; Plato translated by Benjamin Jowett (both public domain)
source.lead_en: Two short passages, one from each side, written two thousand years apart.
source.lead_zh: 兩段短文，一邊一段，寫作的時間相隔兩千年。

passages.en: Let us then suppose the mind to be, as we say, white paper, void of all characters, without any ideas:—How comes it to be furnished? … Whence has it all the MATERIALS of reason and knowledge? To this I answer, in one word, from EXPERIENCE.
passages.zh: 那麼讓我們假設，心靈就像我們所說的那樣，是一張白紙，上面沒有任何記號，沒有任何觀念：它是怎麼被填滿的？……它那全部理性與知識的「材料」是從哪裡來的？對此我用一個詞回答：來自「經驗」。
passages.note_en: Two words deserve attention. The first is “suppose”: Locke offers the white paper as a hypothesis to be tested by how much it can explain. The second is “materials.” He says that experience supplies the materials of knowledge. He does not say that it supplies the mind’s ability to work on them, and elsewhere he takes that ability for granted. (“Characters” here means written marks, and “whence” means “from where.”)
passages.note_zh: 有兩個詞值得注意。第一個是「假設」：洛克提出白紙，是當作一個假說，要用它能解釋多少來檢驗。第二個是「材料」。他說經驗供應知識的材料；他並沒有說，經驗供應了心靈加工這些材料的能力，而他在別處把那種能力視為理所當然。（這裡的 characters 是「寫下的記號」，whence 是「從哪裡」。）

passages.en: …for as all nature is akin, and the soul has learned all things; there is no difficulty in her eliciting or as men say learning, out of a single recollection all the rest, if a man is strenuous and does not faint; for all enquiry and all learning is but recollection.
passages.zh: ……因為整個自然是相通的，而靈魂已經學過一切；所以只要一個人奮勉而不氣餒，要她從一次回憶引出其餘的一切——也就是人們所說的「學習」——並沒有困難；因為一切探究、一切學習，都不過是回憶。
passages.note_en: The phrase to notice is “as all nature is akin.” Plato’s claim is that knowledge forms a connected whole, so that recovering one piece gives a hold on the rest. That part of the doctrine does not depend on a previous life, and anyone who has watched a student suddenly see how two topics fit together will recognize it. Note also the moral: “if a man is strenuous.” The theory was offered to Meno as a reason not to give up inquiring.
passages.note_zh: 要注意的詞組是「整個自然是相通的」。柏拉圖的主張是：知識構成一個彼此相連的整體，所以找回一塊，就抓得住其餘的。這一部分的學說並不依賴前世；凡是看過學生忽然看出兩個主題怎麼接在一起的人，都認得這件事。也注意它的寓意：「只要一個人奮勉」。這個理論是提給美諾的，當作不要放棄探究的理由。

items.o_en: The slave boy proves nothing. Socrates asks leading questions and draws the crucial figure himself. The boy was taught, by a very good teacher.
items.o_zh: 那個少年什麼也沒證明。蘇格拉底問的是誘導性的問題，而且關鍵的那個圖是他自己畫的。少年是被教會的，而且老師很高明。
items.r_en: The objection is fair as far as the discovery goes: the boy would not have found the diagonal alone. But Plato’s point concerns what happens next. When the figure is drawn, the boy does not take the answer on trust. He sees for himself that it is right and could not be otherwise. That act of seeing was not supplied by the teacher, and it is what needs explaining.
items.r_zh: 就「發現」這件事而言，這個反駁是公允的：少年靠自己找不到那條對角線。但柏拉圖的重點在於接下來發生的事。圖畫出來之後，少年並不是憑信任接受答案。他自己看出那是對的，而且不可能是別的樣子。這個「看出來」的動作不是老師供應的，而需要解釋的正是它。

items.o_en: Talk of innate ideas is dangerous. It has always been used to declare some people naturally superior and some beliefs beyond criticism.
items.o_zh: 「天生觀念」的說法是危險的。它一向被用來宣稱某些人天生優越、某些信念不容批評。
items.r_en: This was part of Locke’s motive, and the history bears him out. The reply is that the blank slate has been abused as well, by regimes that believed human beings could be remade to order. A doctrine’s political uses do not settle whether it is true. They are a reason to be careful about which claims of innateness we accept, and to demand evidence for each.
items.r_zh: 這是洛克的動機之一，而歷史證實了他的擔憂。回應是：白板說同樣被濫用過，濫用它的是那些相信人可以照訂單重新製造的政權。一個學說在政治上被怎麼用，並不能決定它是不是真的。那是一個理由，要我們小心自己接受哪些「天生」的主張，並且對每一個都要求證據。

items.o_en: The whole debate rests on a false choice. Asking whether knowledge comes from nature or from experience is like asking whether the area of a rectangle comes from its length or its width.
items.o_zh: 整場辯論建立在一個假的二選一上。問知識來自天性還是來自經驗，就像問長方形的面積來自長還是來自寬。
items.r_en: Most researchers would now agree, and Kant said something similar. But the particular questions remain open and are worth asking one at a time. How much of grammar is built in? Is there an inborn sense of number, of fairness, of cause? “Both” is the right general answer, and it tells us nothing about any particular case.
items.r_zh: 現在多數研究者會同意，而康德說過類似的話。但個別的問題仍然沒有定論，而且值得一個一個地問。文法有多少是內建的？有沒有天生的數感、公平感、因果感？「兩者都有」是正確的總答案，而它對任何個別的情況什麼也沒說。

said.claim: Locke said the mind is a tabula rasa.
said.claim_zh: 洛克說心靈是一塊 tabula rasa（白板）。
said.en: The Latin phrase, meaning a scraped writing tablet, does not appear in the Essay. Locke’s images there are “white paper” and an “empty cabinet.” The tablet goes back to Aristotle, who compared the intellect before it thinks to a tablet on which nothing has yet been written, and tabula rasa became the standard term among medieval philosophers. Later writers attached it to Locke because he gave the idea its most influential defense.
said.zh: 這個拉丁詞組的意思是「刮乾淨的書寫板」，在《人類理解論》裡並沒有出現。洛克在那裡用的意象是「白紙」與「空櫃子」。書寫板可以追溯到亞里斯多德，他把尚未思考的理智比作一塊還沒寫上任何東西的板子；tabula rasa 則成了中世紀哲學家的標準用語。後來的作者把它掛在洛克名下，因為這個想法最有影響力的辯護是他提出的。

terms.d_en: The view that all knowledge of the world derives from experience.
terms.d_zh: 主張關於世界的一切知識都來自經驗。

terms.d_en: The view that reason gives us some knowledge independently of experience.
terms.d_zh: 主張理性能給我們某些不依賴經驗的知識。

terms.d_en: Present in the mind by nature, whether as knowledge or as a disposition.
terms.d_zh: 出於本性而在心靈之中的，不論是作為知識還是作為傾向。

terms.o: L. ‘from what comes before’ / ‘from what comes after’
terms.d_en: Knowable independently of experience; knowable only through experience.
terms.d_zh: 不依賴經驗而可知的；只有透過經驗才可知的。

terms.d_en: Plato’s doctrine that learning is the recovery of knowledge the soul already has.
terms.d_zh: 柏拉圖的學說：學習是找回靈魂已有的知識。

terms.d_en: Locke’s two sources of ideas: the senses, and the mind’s awareness of its own operations.
terms.d_zh: 洛克的兩個觀念來源：感官，以及心靈對自身運作的察覺。

terms.d_en: A standing tendency to act or think in a certain way when the occasion arises.
terms.d_zh: 機緣出現時，以某種方式行動或思考的持續趨向。

terms.d_en: The modern view that the mind has substantial inborn structure.
terms.d_zh: 現代的看法：心靈有相當多的天生結構。

terms.d_en: Chomsky’s argument that children know more about language than their experience could have taught them.
terms.d_zh: 喬姆斯基的論證：孩子對語言的了解，多過他們的經驗所能教給他們的。

vocab.eg: Experiments now bear on the dispute.
vocab.eg_zh: 現在有實驗可以介入這場爭論。

vocab.eg: The demonstration is harder to dismiss than the explanation.
vocab.eg_zh: 那場示範比那個解釋更難打發。

vocab.eg: How comes the mind to be furnished?
vocab.eg_zh: 心靈是怎麼被填滿的？

vocab.eg: No principles are stamped on the mind at birth.
vocab.eg_zh: 沒有任何原則在出生時就印在心靈上。

vocab.eg: Leibniz granted that nothing is in the intellect which was not first in the senses.
vocab.eg_zh: 萊布尼茲承認，凡在理智中的，無不先在感官中。

vocab.eg: The sculptor’s blows are needed to bring the figure out.
vocab.eg_zh: 要把雕像顯現出來，需要雕刻家的敲擊。

vocab.eg: Xunzi held that our nature would otherwise run to conflict.
vocab.eg_zh: 荀子認為，我們的本性否則會走向爭奪。

vocab.eg: That some framework is needed is now close to common ground.
vocab.eg_zh: 「需要某種框架」現在已經接近共識。

vocab.eg: The children had no ready-made knowledge linking sight to touch.
vocab.eg_zh: 那些孩子沒有現成的、把視覺連到觸覺的知識。

vocab.eg: A sprout has a nature of its own and still has to be tended.
vocab.eg_zh: 芽有它自己的本性，卻仍然需要照料。

quiz.q: What does Plato take the slave boy’s success to show?
options: That learning is the recovery of knowledge the soul already has.
That slaves were secretly educated in Athens.
That geometry depends on measurement.
That Socrates was a poor teacher.

quiz.q: According to Locke, what are the two sources of all our ideas?
options: Sensation and reflection.
Reason and revelation.
Memory and imagination.
Nature and custom.

quiz.q: What is Leibniz’s image of a block of marble with veins meant to show?
options: The mind has inborn tendencies that experience brings out.
The mind is completely blank at birth.
Sculpture is the highest art.
Experience contributes nothing.

quiz.q: What does Mencius mean by 良知 (innate knowledge)?
options: What people know without having to reflect, such as a child’s love for its parents.
Knowledge acquired through long study of the classics.
The rules of ritual.
Skill in debate.

quiz.q: What did the 2011 test of Molyneux’s question find?
options: Newly sighted children could not at first match sight to touch, and learned to within days.
They matched the objects immediately.
They never learned to match them.
The test could not be carried out.

write.en: Think of something you know that you cannot remember being taught, such as a rule of your own language. How do you think you came to know it?
write.zh: 想一件你知道、卻不記得有人教過你的事，例如你母語的某條規則。你認為自己是怎麼知道它的？

write.en: As a teacher or a parent, do you act more like Locke or more like Leibniz? Give one example from your own practice, in about 150 words.
write.zh: 身為老師或父母，你的做法比較像洛克，還是比較像萊布尼茲？用大約 150 個英文字，舉一個你自己實務上的例子。

write.en: Was the slave boy taught or reminded? Defend one answer and say what evidence would change your mind.
write.zh: 那個少年是被教會的，還是被提醒的？為其中一個答案辯護，並說出什麼證據會讓你改變想法。

paras.en: Buddhist thought contains both positions, and adds a third that neither Locke nor Leibniz considered. The empiricist strand is early and strong. Asked to define “the all,” the Buddha lists the eye and forms, the ear and sounds, the nose and odors, the tongue and tastes, the body and tangibles, the mind and mental objects, and says that anyone who claims to describe another “all” beyond these is speaking of what lies outside his range (Saṃyutta Nikāya 35.23). Knowledge begins from contact at the six sense bases, and mind is counted as a sixth sense, which is not far from Locke’s sensation and reflection.
paras.zh: 佛教思想裡兩種立場都有，還多了第三種，是洛克與萊布尼茲都沒考慮過的。經驗主義的這一脈出現得早，而且很強。有人請佛陀界定「一切」，佛陀列出：眼與色、耳與聲、鼻與香、舌與味、身與觸、意與法；並且說，誰要是宣稱在這些之外另有一個「一切」，那就是在談超出他範圍的東西（《相應部》35.23）。知識始於六處的「觸」；而意被算作第六個感官，這跟洛克的感覺與反省相去不遠。

paras.en: The other strand resembles Mencius. An early text says that the mind is luminous and is defiled by visiting defilements (Aṅguttara Nikāya 1.49). The Mahāyāna doctrine of buddha-nature develops the thought: awakening is not manufactured, it is uncovered. When Huineng awakens in the Platform Sūtra he exclaims, “Who would have thought that my own nature is complete in itself from the beginning!” (何期自性，本自具足). And the third position comes from rebirth. On the Buddhist account a newborn is not a blank, because it arrives carrying dispositions (vāsanā) laid down by earlier action. This is Plato’s answer, experience before birth, with one difference. What is carried over consists of habits and tendencies, good and bad, and includes no knowledge of eternal truths (Dharma and the West, D12).
paras.zh: 另一脈近似孟子。一部早期的經說：這個心是明淨的，而它被客塵煩惱所染污（《增支部》1.49）。大乘的佛性（如來藏）學說發展了這個想法：覺悟不是製造出來的，是被揭開的。在《六祖壇經》裡，惠能開悟時驚嘆：「何期自性，本自具足！」第三種立場則來自輪迴。照佛教的說法，新生兒不是空白的，因為它來的時候帶著由過去的行為留下的習氣（vāsanā）。這是柏拉圖的答案——出生之前的經驗——只有一點不同：被帶過來的是習慣與傾向，有好有壞，其中並沒有對永恆真理的知識（佛法與西方哲學 D12）。

further.t: Plato, Meno, translated by Benjamin Jowett
further.n_en: The geometry lesson is at 82b–85b; read it with a pencil.
further.n_zh: 幾何課在 82b–85b；手上拿枝筆讀。

further.t: John Locke, An Essay Concerning Human Understanding, Book I, chapter 2, and Book II, chapter 1
further.n_en: The attack on innate principles, and the white paper.
further.n_zh: 對天生原則的攻擊，以及白紙。

further.t: G. W. Leibniz, New Essays on Human Understanding, Preface
further.n_en: Ten pages; the marble, and the reply to Locke in outline.
further.n_zh: 十頁；大理石的比喻，以及對洛克回應的綱要。

further.t: Mencius 6A and 7A (告子上、盡心上)
further.n_en: The debate with Gaozi about human nature.
further.n_zh: 與告子關於人性的辯論。

further.t: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, “Rationalism vs. Empiricism” and “Molyneux’s Problem”

lessons.title: Will the Sun Rise Tomorrow?
lessons.blurb_en: Hume’s problem of induction: why no amount of past experience can prove anything about the future, and why we go on trusting it all the same.
lessons.blurb_zh: 休謨的歸納問題：為什麼再多的過往經驗，也無法對未來證明任何事；以及為什麼我們照樣繼續信任它。
lessons.big_en: Every belief about what we have not observed rests on the assumption that nature will go on as before. That assumption cannot be proved by logic and cannot be proved by experience without circularity.
lessons.big_zh: 我們對未曾觀察之事的每一個信念，都建立在「自然會照舊運行」這個假定上。這個假定無法用邏輯證明；用經驗來證明，又免不了循環。

essay.h_en: The safest bet in the world

paras.en: Nothing seems more certain than that the sun will rise tomorrow. Ask how you know it, and the first answer is that it always has. Ask why that is a reason, and the answer is that things which have always happened go on happening. Ask how you know that, and the honest reply is that it has always been so in the past. At this point the same reason has been given twice. David Hume noticed the repetition in the 1730s, when he was in his twenties, and nobody has found a way out of it that everyone accepts.
paras.zh: 沒有什麼事看起來比「明天太陽會升起」更確定。問你怎麼知道，第一個答案是：它一向如此。問這為什麼算是理由，答案是：一向發生的事會繼續發生。再問你怎麼知道這一點，誠實的回答是：過去一向是這樣。到這裡，同一個理由已經給了兩次。休謨在 1730 年代注意到這個重複，當時他才二十幾歲；至今沒有人找到一條人人接受的出路。

paras.en: Hume begins by sorting everything we can know into two kinds. Relations of ideas are truths such as “three times five is equal to the half of thirty.” They can be established by thinking alone, and to deny one is to contradict oneself. Matters of fact are truths such as “the sun is shining.” They can be learned only from experience, and the denial of any of them is perfectly conceivable. His example has become famous: “That the sun will not rise to-morrow is no less intelligible a proposition, and implies no more contradiction than the affirmation, that it will rise.” So no matter of fact can be proved by pure reasoning. If we know the sun will rise, we know it from experience.
paras.zh: 休謨一開始，把我們能知道的一切分成兩類。「觀念的關係」是像「三乘五等於三十的一半」這樣的真理；它們光靠思考就能確立，否定其中任何一個就會自相矛盾。「實際的事情」是像「太陽正照耀著」這樣的真理；它們只能從經驗得知，而它們當中任何一個的否定，都完全可以設想。他舉的例子後來很有名：「『明天太陽不會升起』這個命題，並不比『它會升起』這個斷言更難理解，也沒有蘊含更多的矛盾。」所以，沒有任何實際的事情可以靠純粹的推理來證明。如果我們知道太陽會升起，那是從經驗知道的。

essay.h_en: What we see when one ball hits another
essay.h_zh: 一顆球撞上另一顆時，我們看見了什麼

paras.en: Experience tells us directly only about what we are now perceiving or remember. To get beyond that, to the fire in the next room or the eclipse next year, we reason from cause to effect. Hume therefore asks what we observe when we observe one thing causing another. One billiard ball rolls toward a second; they touch; the second moves. We see the first motion, the contact, and the second motion. We do not see any power in the first ball that forces the second to move. A person who had never seen bodies collide could not tell, from looking at the first ball, what would happen. What experience adds is repetition: events of the first kind have always been followed by events of the second. He calls this constant conjunction. The idea that the effect must follow is something we supply ourselves.
paras.zh: 經驗直接告訴我們的，只有我們此刻知覺到的、或記得的事。要越過這個範圍，推到隔壁房間的火、明年的日食，我們靠的是從原因到結果的推理。所以休謨問：當我們觀察到一件事「造成」另一件事時，我們到底觀察到了什麼？一顆撞球滾向第二顆；兩者接觸；第二顆動了。我們看見第一個運動、接觸、第二個運動。我們並沒有看見第一顆球裡有什麼「力量」，逼得第二顆非動不可。一個從沒見過物體碰撞的人，光看第一顆球，是說不出會發生什麼的。經驗添上的是重複：第一類事件之後，總是跟著第二類事件。他把這稱為「恆常連結」。至於「結果必定跟著發生」這個觀念，是我們自己添上去的。

paras.en: Now the problem can be stated exactly. All our conclusions from experience take the form: such things have always gone together, so they will go together again. That step is valid only with an extra premise, that the future will resemble the past. How might the premise be established? It is not a relation of ideas, since a change in the course of nature is conceivable. It must then be a matter of fact, known from experience. But “all inferences from experience suppose, as their foundation, that the future will resemble the past.” To argue that nature will be uniform because it has been uniform so far is to use the principle in order to prove the principle. In Hume’s words, it “is begging the question.”
paras.zh: 現在可以把問題精確地說出來了。我們從經驗得出的一切結論，都是這個形式：這些事一向相伴出現，所以它們會再度相伴出現。這一步要有效，需要一個額外的前提：未來會與過去相似。這個前提要怎麼確立？它不是觀念的關係，因為自然進程的改變是可以設想的。那它就必定是實際的事情，要從經驗得知。可是「一切從經驗出發的推論，都預設未來會與過去相似，以此作為基礎」。主張「自然會保持齊一，因為它到目前為止都是齊一的」，就是用這個原則來證明這個原則。用休謨的話說，這「是乞題」。

paras.en: Notice what the argument does and does not claim. Hume does not say that the sun will fail to rise, or that expecting it is foolish. He says that the expectation is not produced by any argument, because no good argument for it exists.
paras.zh: 注意這個論證主張了什麼、沒有主張什麼。休謨沒有說太陽將不會升起，也沒有說期待它升起是愚蠢的。他說的是：這個期待不是由任何論證產生的，因為根本沒有支持它的好論證。

paras.en: If reasoning does not produce our expectations, what does? Hume’s answer is habit. After seeing two kinds of event joined many times, the mind passes from one to the other automatically, and feels that passage as necessity. “Custom, then, is the great guide of human life. It is that principle alone which renders our experience useful to us.” Infants and animals learn from experience in just this way, and nobody supposes that they do it by constructing arguments. Hume calls this a skeptical solution, because it explains why we believe and leaves the question of justification where it was. He was content with that. Nature, he observed, has not left so important a matter to our fallible reasoning.
paras.zh: 如果產生我們期待的不是推理，那是什麼？休謨的答案是習慣。看見兩類事件多次相連之後，心靈就自動地從一個過渡到另一個，並且把這個過渡感受為必然。「所以，習慣是人類生活的偉大嚮導。唯獨這個原則，使我們的經驗對我們有用。」嬰兒與動物正是這樣從經驗學習的，而沒有人認為牠們是靠建構論證辦到的。休謨把這稱為「懷疑論的解決」，因為它解釋了我們為什麼相信，卻讓證成的問題留在原地。他對此感到滿意。他說，這麼重要的事，自然並沒有交給我們那容易出錯的推理。

paras.en: Bertrand Russell gave the problem its most memorable form. A chicken is fed by the farmer every morning of its life and comes to expect its food when he appears. “The man who has fed the chicken every day throughout its life at last wrings its neck instead, showing that more refined views as to the uniformity of nature would have been useful to the chicken.” The chicken’s reasoning was the same as ours about the sunrise. Europeans were in a similar position with “all swans are white,” on the evidence of every swan anyone had seen, until black swans were found in Australia in 1697.
paras.zh: 羅素給了這個問題最令人難忘的形式。一隻雞，一輩子每天早上都由農夫餵食，於是一見他出現就期待食物。「那個在雞的一生中每天餵牠的人，最後卻扭斷了牠的脖子；這表明，對自然的齊一性若有更精細的看法，對這隻雞會很有用。」這隻雞的推理，跟我們對日出的推理是一樣的。歐洲人對「所有天鵝都是白的」也曾處在類似的位置上，憑的是任何人見過的每一隻天鵝；直到 1697 年在澳洲發現了黑天鵝。

paras.en: Chinese tradition supplies a pair of stories that mark the two ways of going wrong. In the Han Feizi a farmer sees a hare run into a tree stump and break its neck, and he puts down his plow and waits by the stump for another (守株待兔). He has generalized from a single case. In the Liezi a man of Qi cannot eat or sleep for fear that the sky will fall (杞人憂天). He refuses to rely on any regularity at all. Everyone agrees that good sense lies somewhere between the two. Hume’s point is that we cannot prove where.
paras.zh: 中國的傳統提供了一對故事，正好標出兩種走錯的方式。在《韓非子》裡，一個農夫看見一隻兔子撞上樹樁、折斷了脖子，於是放下犁，守在樹樁旁等下一隻（守株待兔）。他是從單一個案做了概括。在《列子》裡，一個杞國人因為害怕天會塌下來而寢食難安（杞人憂天）。他拒絕倚賴任何規律。人人都同意，明智的做法在兩者之間的某處。休謨的重點是：我們無法證明是在哪裡。

paras.en: Hume’s problem has been called the scandal of philosophy, and the attempts to answer it fall into four groups. Kant held that causality is not learned from experience at all. It is a form the mind imposes, a condition of having any ordered experience, and so it is guaranteed to hold of whatever we can experience. Karl Popper accepted Hume’s argument and concluded that science does not use induction. Scientists make bold guesses and try to refute them, and a theory that survives is never thereby shown to be true or even probable. Hans Reichenbach offered a practical defense. We cannot know that nature is uniform, but if it is, induction will find the pattern, and if it is not, no method will work, so we lose nothing by using it. And P. F. Strawson argued that the demand is confused. To ask whether it is reasonable to rely on induction is like asking whether the law is legal: relying on past experience is part of what “reasonable” means.
paras.zh: 休謨的問題被稱為「哲學的醜聞」；回答它的嘗試可以分成四組。康德主張，因果性根本不是從經驗學來的。它是心靈加上去的形式，是擁有任何有秩序的經驗的條件；所以對我們所能經驗的一切，它保證成立。波普接受休謨的論證，並且推出：科學並不使用歸納。科學家提出大膽的猜測，再設法反駁它們；一個存活下來的理論，並不因此就被證明為真，甚至也沒有被證明為很可能為真。萊辛巴哈提出一種實用的辯護：我們無法知道自然是不是齊一的；但如果它是，歸納法會找到那個規律；如果它不是，任何方法都不管用；所以用歸納法，我們什麼也不會損失。史陶生則論證，這個要求本身就搞混了。問「倚賴歸納是否合理」，就像問「法律是否合法」：倚賴過往經驗，本來就是「合理」這個詞的一部分意思。

paras.en: Each reply has its critics, and in 1955 Nelson Goodman made the problem harder. Call an object “grue” if it is first examined before the year 2100 and is green, or is not examined before then and is blue. Every emerald seen so far has been green, and every one has also been grue. Yet we expect future emeralds to be green and not grue. Even if induction is granted, then, something must tell us which patterns to project, and that further rule cannot come from the evidence, which fits both.
paras.zh: 每一種回應都有批評者；而在 1955 年，古德曼把問題弄得更難了。把一個東西稱為「綠藍」（grue），如果它在 2100 年之前首次被檢視而且是綠的，或者在那之前沒被檢視過而且是藍的。迄今見過的每一顆祖母綠都是綠的，也都是「綠藍」的。然而我們預期未來的祖母綠是綠的，不是「綠藍」的。所以，就算承認了歸納法，還是得有什麼東西告訴我們該投射哪些規律；而這條進一步的規則，不可能來自證據，因為證據跟兩者都相符。

paras.en: What should one conclude? Not that anything goes. Hume himself drew a sober moral: “A wise man … proportions his belief to the evidence.” The lesson of the problem is that evidence comes in degrees and never amounts to proof. Scientific laws are the best-supported expectations we have, and they remain expectations. This is the second unit’s conclusion, and it matches the first. Logic could tell us that our premises conflict and could not tell us which to give up. Experience can tell us what has happened so far, and what will happen next is something we infer at our own risk. The sun will rise tomorrow. You are right to be sure of it, and you cannot say why without assuming it.
paras.zh: 該得出什麼結論？不是「怎樣都行」。休謨自己引出了一個清醒的教訓：「有智慧的人……使他的信念與證據成比例。」這個問題的教訓是：證據有程度之分，而且永遠不等於證明。科學定律是我們擁有的、根據最充分的期待，而它們仍然是期待。這是第二單元的結論，而它跟第一單元的結論相呼應。邏輯能告訴我們前提互相衝突，卻不能告訴我們該放棄哪一個。經驗能告訴我們到目前為止發生了什麼；至於接下來會發生什麼，那是我們自負風險去推論的。明天太陽會升起。你對此有把握是對的；而你說不出為什麼，除非先假定它。

lab.title_zh: 親手做一次：那隻雞的推理
lab.lead_en: Be the chicken. Each morning the farmer comes. Watch your confidence grow as the evidence piles up, and notice that the method you are using is the one you use for the sunrise. Then try to justify it.
lab.lead_zh: 你來當那隻雞。每天早上農夫都會來。看著你的信心隨著證據累積而上升，並且留意：你用的方法，就是你對日出用的方法。然後試著替它找理由。

end.en: This morning the farmer wrings your neck. Every one of your observations was accurate, and your confidence had never been higher than it was last night.
end.zh: 今天早上，農夫扭斷了你的脖子。你的每一次觀察都是準確的；而你的信心，從來沒有比昨晚更高過。

rule.en: Confidence here follows a rule of Laplace’s: after n mornings with grain and none without, expect grain tomorrow with probability (n + 1) / (n + 2). The rule itself assumes that tomorrow is drawn from the same process as the days before.
rule.zh: 這裡的信心照拉普拉斯的一條規則計算：連續 n 個早上有穀子、沒有例外，則明天有穀子的機率是 (n + 1) / (n + 2)。這條規則本身就假定：明天跟之前的日子，出自同一個過程。

q.en: Now defend the method. Why is it reasonable to expect the future to resemble the past?
q.zh: 現在替這個方法辯護。為什麼期待未來會與過去相似，是合理的？

t.en: Because relying on past experience has always worked before.
t.zh: 因為倚賴過往經驗，以前一向行得通。

r.en: That it worked before is a fact about the past. To conclude that it will work in future, you must assume that the future will resemble the past, which is the thing to be proved.
r.zh: 它以前行得通，是關於過去的事實。要推出它以後也行得通，你必須假定未來會與過去相似，而這正是要證明的事。

t.en: Because it is a truth of logic.
t.zh: 因為這是邏輯上的真理。

r.en: A truth of logic cannot be denied without contradiction. “The course of nature will change tomorrow” is false, we hope, but it is not contradictory. You can picture it happening.
r.zh: 邏輯真理是不能否定的，否定就會自相矛盾。「自然的進程明天會改變」——我們希望它是假的——但它並不矛盾。你想像得出它發生的樣子。

t.en: Because the laws of nature guarantee it.
t.zh: 因為自然定律保證如此。

r.en: How do we know the laws will hold tomorrow? We know only that they have held so far. A law of nature is a regularity projected into the future, so it cannot be used to justify the projecting.
r.zh: 我們怎麼知道定律明天還成立？我們只知道它們到目前為止都成立。自然定律本身就是被投射到未來的規律，所以不能拿它來證成這個投射。

t.en: I cannot justify it. I simply find that I expect it.
t.zh: 我沒辦法證成它。我只是發現自己這樣期待。

r.en: This is where Hume ends: “Custom, then, is the great guide of human life.” Whether one should be content to stop here is what Kant, Popper, Reichenbach, and Strawson disagree about.
r.zh: 休謨就停在這裡：「習慣是人類生活的偉大嚮導。」至於停在這裡該不該滿足，正是康德、波普、萊辛巴哈、史陶生意見分歧的地方。

argument.lead_en: Hume’s reasoning is a dilemma. There are two ways to establish a principle, and he argues that neither is available. Click a step to see what can be said against it.
argument.lead_zh: 休謨的推理是一個兩難。要確立一個原則有兩條路，而他論證兩條都走不通。點任何一步，看看別人可以怎麼反對它。

steps.en: Every inference from what we have observed to what we have not relies on the principle that the future will resemble the past.
steps.zh: 每一個從已觀察之事到未觀察之事的推論，都倚賴「未來會與過去相似」這個原則。
steps.ob_en: Popper denied this. On his account science never infers from the observed to the unobserved. It proposes theories and tests them, and testing uses only deduction. Critics reply that we still rely on well-tested theories when we build bridges, and that this reliance is induction under another name.
steps.ob_zh: 波普否認這一點。照他的說法，科學從來不從已觀察的推到未觀察的。它提出理論並加以檢驗，而檢驗只用到演繹。批評者回答：我們造橋的時候，仍然倚賴經過充分檢驗的理論；而這種倚賴，就是換了名字的歸納。

steps.en: The principle is not a truth of reason, because its denial involves no contradiction.
steps.zh: 這個原則不是理性的真理，因為否定它並不涉及矛盾。
steps.ob_en: Rarely disputed. A world in which regularities break down is describable, however unwelcome.
steps.ob_zh: 很少有爭議。一個規律崩解的世界，不管多麼不受歡迎，都是描述得出來的。

steps.en: The principle cannot be established from experience, because every argument from experience already assumes it.
steps.zh: 這個原則無法從經驗確立，因為每一個從經驗出發的論證，都已經預設了它。
steps.ob_en: Some philosophers accept the circle and deny that it is vicious. We could not persuade a doubter this way, they grant, but a method may still be reliable, and a reliable method can confirm its own reliability. Others find this no better than a fortune-teller vouching for herself.
steps.ob_zh: 有些哲學家承認這個循環，但否認它是惡性的。他們同意，我們沒辦法這樣說服一個懷疑的人；但一種方法仍然可以是可靠的，而可靠的方法可以確認它自己的可靠性。另一些人覺得，這不比算命師替自己掛保證高明。

steps.en: Reasoning from ideas alone and reasoning from experience are the only two ways of establishing anything.
steps.zh: 單從觀念出發的推理，以及從經驗出發的推理，是確立任何事情僅有的兩種方式。
steps.ob_en: This is the step Kant attacked. He proposed a third category: principles that are not true by definition and yet are known independently of experience, because they are conditions of having experience at all. Causality, he argued, is one of them. Whether there is such a category is the central question of his Critique of Pure Reason.
steps.ob_zh: 康德攻擊的是這一步。他提出第三個範疇：有些原則並不是憑定義為真，卻又是不依賴經驗而被知道的，因為它們是「擁有經驗」本身的條件。他論證，因果性就是其中之一。到底有沒有這樣的範疇，是他《純粹理性批判》的核心問題。

steps.en: Therefore our beliefs about what we have not observed are not founded on reasoning. They are produced by custom.
steps.zh: 所以，我們對未觀察之事的信念，並不是建立在推理上的。它們是習慣產生的。
steps.ob_en: Even those who accept the argument disagree about how much it shows. One reading is that induction is unjustified. Another is that the demand for a justification from outside was a mistake.
steps.ob_zh: 就算是接受這個論證的人，對它證明了多少也意見不一。一種讀法是：歸納沒有得到證成。另一種讀法是：要求一個「從外面來的」證成，本身就是錯的。

source.work: David Hume, An Enquiry Concerning Human Understanding (1748), sections IV and V
source.work_zh: 休謨《人類理解研究》第四、五章
source.lead_en: Hume first set out the argument in his Treatise of Human Nature, which almost nobody read. The Enquiry is his second attempt, shorter and written to please.
source.lead_zh: 休謨最早是在《人性論》裡提出這個論證的，而那本書幾乎沒有人讀。《人類理解研究》是他的第二次嘗試，比較短，而且是寫來讓人讀得愉快的。

passages.en: That the sun will not rise to-morrow is no less intelligible a proposition, and implies no more contradiction than the affirmation, that it will rise. We should in vain, therefore, attempt to demonstrate its falsehood.
passages.zh: 「明天太陽不會升起」這個命題，並不比「它會升起」這個斷言更難理解，也沒有蘊含更多的矛盾。所以，我們想要論證它為假，是徒勞的。
passages.note_en: The test Hume applies is conceivability. If you can clearly imagine a thing, it involves no contradiction, and if it involves no contradiction, logic cannot rule it out. “Demonstrate” has its strict sense here, to prove with certainty by reasoning alone. He is not saying that there is no evidence for the sunrise. He is saying that the evidence, whatever it is, cannot be a proof.
passages.note_zh: 休謨用的檢驗是「可設想性」。如果你能清楚地想像一件事，它就不涉及矛盾；而如果它不涉及矛盾，邏輯就排除不了它。這裡的 demonstrate 用的是嚴格的意思：單憑推理、確定無疑地證明。他並不是說日出沒有證據。他是說，不管證據是什麼，它都不可能是一個證明。

passages.en: Custom, then, is the great guide of human life. It is that principle alone which renders our experience useful to us, and makes us expect, for the future, a similar train of events with those which have appeared in the past.
passages.zh: 所以，習慣是人類生活的偉大嚮導。唯獨這個原則，使我們的經驗對我們有用，並且使我們期待：未來會出現一連串事件，與過去出現過的相似。
passages.note_en: “Custom” means habit, a tendency produced by repetition. The sentence is carefully balanced. It demotes our reasoning, since the guide of life turns out to be a habit, and at the same time it praises the habit, without which experience would be useless to us. Hume’s skepticism concerns the foundations of our beliefs. He never recommends giving the beliefs up.
passages.note_zh: custom 在這裡的意思是習慣，一種由重複產生的傾向。這個句子拿捏得很仔細。它貶低了我們的推理，因為生活的嚮導原來是一種習慣；同時它又稱讚了這個習慣：沒有它，經驗對我們毫無用處。休謨的懷疑論針對的是我們信念的基礎；他從來不曾建議放棄這些信念。

items.o_en: Induction obviously works. Science built on it has given us vaccines and spacecraft. A method with that record needs no further defense.
items.o_zh: 歸納法顯然行得通。建立在它上面的科學，給了我們疫苗與太空船。有這種紀錄的方法，不需要別的辯護。
items.r_en: This is the most natural reply, and it is the circle again. The record shows that induction has worked. To conclude that it will go on working is an inductive inference. Hume never denied the record. What he wanted to know was what entitles us to extend it.
items.r_zh: 這是最自然的回應，而它又是那個圓圈。這份紀錄顯示歸納法「一直」行得通。要推出它「將會繼續」行得通，是一個歸納推論。休謨從來沒有否認這份紀錄。他想知道的是：我們憑什麼有資格把它延伸下去。

items.o_en: The problem only shows that induction is not deduction. Of course past evidence does not entail future events. Probable reasoning was never supposed to give certainty.
items.o_zh: 這個問題只是顯示歸納不是演繹。過去的證據當然不蘊涵未來的事件。或然的推理，本來就不是要給人確定性的。
items.r_en: Hume would accept the first sentence and deny that it disposes of the difficulty. His argument applies to probability too. To say that past observations make a future event likely, we must assume that past frequencies are a guide to future ones, and that is the same principle in a weaker form.
items.r_zh: 休謨會接受第一句話，但否認這樣就解決了困難。他的論證對或然性同樣適用。要說過去的觀察使某個未來事件「很可能」發生，我們必須假定過去的頻率是未來頻率的指引；而這是同一個原則，只是比較弱的形式。

items.o_en: If the argument were sound, we could never choose between a physicist and a fortune-teller. Since we plainly can, the argument must contain a mistake.
items.o_zh: 如果這個論證是健全的，我們就永遠無法在物理學家與算命師之間做選擇。既然我們顯然可以，這個論證裡一定有錯。
items.r_en: This is Moore’s move from the lesson on dreaming, applied to induction, and many philosophers think it is right. But knowing that a mistake exists is different from finding it. After nearly three centuries there is no agreement about which premise fails. That is a reason to regard the problem as deep. It is no reason to stop consulting physicists.
items.r_zh: 這是「夢」那一課裡摩爾的那一招，用在歸納上；許多哲學家認為它是對的。但知道有一個錯誤存在，跟找到它是兩回事。將近三百年過去了，對於是哪一個前提出錯，仍然沒有共識。這是把這個問題看得很深的理由；這並不是不再請教物理學家的理由。

said.claim_zh: 「非凡的主張需要非凡的證據。」（休謨）
said.en: The slogan in this form comes from the astronomer Carl Sagan’s television series Cosmos. It is often described as “Hume’s maxim,” and the thought is certainly Hume’s. What he wrote, in his essay on miracles, is the plainer sentence quoted above: “A wise man, therefore, proportions his belief to the evidence.”
said.zh: 這個說法的這種形式，出自天文學家卡爾・薩根的電視影集《宇宙》。它常被稱為「休謨的箴言」，而這個想法確實是休謨的。他在論神蹟的那一章裡寫下的，是上面引過的那個比較平實的句子：「所以，有智慧的人使他的信念與證據成比例。」

terms.d_en: Reasoning from observed cases to unobserved ones, or to a general law.
terms.d_zh: 從觀察過的個案，推到未觀察的個案，或推到普遍的定律。

terms.t: relations of ideas / matters of fact
terms.zh: 觀念的關係／實際的事情
terms.d_en: Hume’s two kinds of truth: those whose denial is contradictory, and those known only from experience. The division is called Hume’s fork.
terms.d_zh: 休謨的兩類真理：否定它就會矛盾的，以及只能從經驗得知的。這個劃分稱為「休謨之叉」。

terms.d_en: The principle that unobserved cases will resemble observed ones.
terms.d_zh: 未觀察的個案會與已觀察的個案相似，這個原則。

terms.d_en: The regular following of one kind of event by another, which is all we observe of causation.
terms.d_zh: 一類事件之後規律地跟著另一類事件；這就是我們對因果所觀察到的全部。

terms.d_en: The supposed tie by which a cause forces its effect, of which Hume says we have no impression.
terms.d_zh: 原因「逼出」結果的那個假想的紐帶；休謨說，我們對它沒有任何印象。

terms.d_en: In Hume, the habit of expectation produced by repeated experience.
terms.d_zh: 在休謨，指由重複的經驗產生的期待習慣。

terms.d_en: Popper’s account of scientific method: theories cannot be proved, only refuted.
terms.d_zh: 波普對科學方法的說明：理論無法被證明，只能被反駁。

terms.d_en: Goodman’s invented predicate, used to show that evidence alone does not tell us which regularities to project.
terms.d_zh: 古德曼發明的謂詞，用來說明：單憑證據，不足以告訴我們該投射哪些規律。

vocab.eg: Nobody has found a way out of it that everyone accepts.
vocab.eg_zh: 沒有人找到一條人人接受的出路。

vocab.eg: That the sun will not rise is no less intelligible a proposition.
vocab.eg_zh: 「太陽不會升起」並不是比較難理解的命題。

vocab.eg: We should in vain attempt to demonstrate its falsehood.
vocab.eg_zh: 我們想要論證它為假，是徒勞的。

vocab.eg: The idea that the effect must follow is something we supply ourselves.
vocab.eg_zh: 「結果必定跟著發生」這個觀念，是我們自己添上去的。

vocab.eg: Custom alone renders our experience useful to us.
vocab.eg_zh: 唯獨習慣，使我們的經驗對我們有用。

vocab.eg: Hume was content with a skeptical solution.
vocab.eg_zh: 休謨滿足於一個懷疑論的解決。

vocab.eg: Hume drew a sober moral from the problem.
vocab.eg_zh: 休謨從這個問題引出了一個清醒的教訓。

vocab.eg: A wise man proportions his belief to the evidence.
vocab.eg_zh: 有智慧的人使他的信念與證據成比例。

vocab.eg: Evidence comes in degrees and never amounts to proof.
vocab.eg_zh: 證據有程度之分，而且永遠不等於證明。

vocab.eg: What will happen next is something we infer at our own risk.
vocab.eg_zh: 接下來會發生什麼，是我們自負風險去推論的。

quiz.q: Why, according to Hume, can it not be proved by reasoning alone that the sun will rise?
options: Because its not rising is conceivable without contradiction.
Because astronomers disagree about it.
Because the sun is too far away to study.
Because reasoning is always mistaken.

quiz.q: What do we actually observe when one billiard ball strikes another?
options: One motion, a contact, and a second motion, with no power connecting them.
A force passing from the first ball into the second.
The law of nature that governs collisions.
Nothing at all.

quiz.q: Why is it circular to justify induction by its past success?
options: The step from past success to future success is itself an inductive inference.
Induction has never succeeded.
Circles are used in geometry.
Success cannot be measured.

quiz.q: What is Hume’s own “skeptical solution”?
options: Our expectations are produced by custom, with no argument behind them.
God guarantees the uniformity of nature.
We should stop expecting anything.
Induction is a form of deduction.

quiz.q: What does Goodman’s “grue” add to the problem?
options: Evidence alone does not tell us which regularities to project into the future.
Emeralds are really blue.
Colors cannot be known.
Induction works only for colors.

write.en: Describe a belief about tomorrow that you hold with complete confidence. List your evidence for it, then say what principle carries you from the evidence to the belief.
write.zh: 描述一個你完全有把握的、關於明天的信念。列出你的證據，然後說出是什麼原則把你從證據帶到這個信念。

write.en: Which of the four replies (Kant, Popper, Reichenbach, Strawson) do you find most convincing? Defend it in about 150 words against one objection.
write.zh: 四種回應（康德、波普、萊辛巴哈、史陶生）裡，你覺得哪一個最有說服力？用大約 150 個英文字，針對一個反駁為它辯護。

write.en: Think of a time when you were the chicken: a regularity you relied on stopped holding. What, if anything, should you have noticed beforehand?
write.zh: 想一次你自己當了那隻雞的經驗：一個你倚賴的規律不再成立。事前你本來應該注意到什麼（如果有的話）？

paras.en: The Buddha’s summary of causation is strikingly spare. “When this exists, that comes to be; with the arising of this, that arises. When this does not exist, that does not come to be; with the cessation of this, that ceases” (Saṃyutta Nikāya 12.61). The formula states a regular dependence between conditions and what they condition. It says nothing about a power or force that passes from one to the other. Hume, analyzing the billiard balls, found constant conjunction and no necessary connection, and a reader of the early texts may feel that the two accounts are describing the same thing. Nāgārjuna later pressed the point as hard as Hume did, arguing that the notion of a cause producing its effect by an inner power cannot be made coherent.
paras.zh: 佛陀對因果的概括，簡省得驚人。「此有故彼有，此生故彼生；此無故彼無，此滅故彼滅」（《相應部》12.61）。這個公式陳述的是條件與被條件者之間一種有規律的依待。它完全沒有提到有什麼力量從一方傳到另一方。休謨分析撞球，找到了恆常連結，沒有找到必然連結；讀早期經典的人也許會覺得，這兩種說法描述的是同一件事。龍樹後來把這一點追問得跟休謨一樣緊，論證說「原因憑內在的力量產生結果」這個概念，沒辦法說得前後一致。

paras.en: The traditions differ over what follows. Hume concludes that our causal beliefs rest on habit and leaves it there. Buddhist philosophers treat the regularity as discoverable and as the basis of the path: because suffering arises from conditions, it ceases when the conditions cease. They were aware of the difficulty. The Indian materialists, the Cārvākas, rejected inference altogether on the ground that no number of observed cases can establish a universal rule, which is Hume’s objection many centuries early. Dharmakīrti’s reply was that some connections are grounded in the natures of things and are not mere regularities, as smoke depends on fire by being produced from it. Whether that reply succeeds is the question of whether Hume can be answered (Dharma and the West, D4 and D13).
paras.zh: 兩個傳統的差別，在於接下來怎麼走。休謨的結論是我們的因果信念建立在習慣上，然後就停在那裡。佛教哲學家則認為這種規律是可以被發現的，而且是道的基礎：因為苦從條件生起，所以條件止息，苦就止息。他們知道這裡有困難。印度的唯物論者順世派（Cārvāka）整個否定了比量（推論），理由是觀察到再多個案，也無法確立一條普遍規則；這是早了許多個世紀的休謨式反駁。法稱的回應是：有些連結是根植於事物的本性的，不只是規律而已，就像煙依待火，是因為煙由火所生。這個回應成不成功，就是「休謨能不能被回答」這個問題（佛法與西方哲學 D4、D13）。

further.t: David Hume, An Enquiry Concerning Human Understanding, sections IV, V, and VII
further.n_en: About forty pages, and among the best prose in philosophy.
further.n_zh: 大約四十頁，是哲學裡最好的散文之一。

further.t: Bertrand Russell, The Problems of Philosophy, chapter 6, “On Induction”
further.n_en: The chicken.
further.n_zh: 那隻雞的出處。

further.t: Karl Popper, Conjectures and Refutations (1963), chapter 1
further.n_en: The case that science does without induction.
further.n_zh: 主張科學不需要歸納法的論述。

further.t: Nelson Goodman, Fact, Fiction, and Forecast (1955), chapter 3
further.n_en: The new riddle of induction, and grue.
further.n_zh: 歸納的新謎題，以及「綠藍」。

further.t: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, “The Problem of Induction”

lessons.title: Is It Still the Same Ship?
lessons.blurb_en: The Ship of Theseus: what it takes for a thing to remain itself while every part of it is replaced.
lessons.blurb_zh: 特修斯之船：一樣東西的每個部分都被換掉了，要憑什麼才算仍然是它自己？
lessons.big_en: Sameness through change can be grounded in matter, in form, in history, or in our own ways of counting. The four give different answers, and each of them breaks down in some case.
lessons.big_zh: 「變化中的同一」可以建立在材料上、形式上、歷史上，或建立在我們自己計數的方式上。這四者給出不同的答案，而每一個都會在某個情況下失靈。

paras.en: With this lesson the subject changes. The last unit asked what we can know. This one asks what there is and what it is like, which is the business of metaphysics, and it begins with a boat. The Athenians believed that they still possessed the ship in which their hero Theseus had sailed back from Crete after killing the Minotaur. Plutarch, writing around 100 CE, reports that it “was preserved by the Athenians down even to the time of Demetrius Phalereus, for they took away the old planks as they decayed, putting in new and stronger timber in their place, insomuch that this ship became a standing example among the philosophers, for the logical question as to things that grow; one side holding that the ship remained the same, and the other contending that it was not the same.”
paras.zh: 從這一課開始，主題換了。上一個單元問的是我們能知道什麼。這個單元問的是：有什麼東西存在、它們是什麼樣子；這是形上學的工作，而它從一艘船開始。雅典人相信，他們仍然保有英雄特修斯殺死米諾陶之後從克里特航行回來的那艘船。普魯塔克大約在西元 100 年寫道，這艘船「被雅典人保存下來，一直到德米特里・法勒魯姆的時代；因為舊木板一朽壞，他們就拆掉，換上新的、更堅固的木料；以致於這艘船在哲學家當中成了一個現成的例子，用來討論關於『會生長的東西』的邏輯問題：一方主張船還是同一艘，另一方堅稱它已經不是同一艘了。」

paras.en: Both sides have a case. Those who say it is the same ship can point out that there was never a day on which Athens had no ship of Theseus. A single plank was changed, and the ship with one new plank was surely the ship that had been there the day before. The next repair was no different. If the ship survives each step, it survives all of them. Those who say it is not the same can point to the result. Not one splinter that Theseus touched is left. A thing made wholly of timber he never saw can be a faithful replica of his ship, and a replica is a different thing from the original.
paras.zh: 雙方都有道理。主張是同一艘船的人可以指出：雅典從來沒有哪一天是沒有特修斯之船的。換掉了一塊木板，而換了一塊新木板的船，當然就是前一天在那裡的那艘船。下一次修補也沒有什麼不同。如果這艘船撐得過每一步，它就撐得過全部的步驟。主張不是同一艘的人可以指著結果說：特修斯碰過的木頭，連一根碎片都不剩。一個完全用他從沒見過的木料做成的東西，可以是他那艘船的忠實複製品，而複製品跟原物是兩樣東西。

essay.h_zh: 霍布斯把事情弄得更糟

paras.en: In 1655 Thomas Hobbes added a twist that turned an old puzzle into a hard one. Suppose that someone had kept the old planks as they were taken out, and afterward put them together again in the same order. Now there are two ships. One stands in the harbor, where the ship of Theseus has always stood, and it grew out of the original by gradual repair. The other stands in a warehouse, and it is made of exactly the planks that Theseus sailed on, arranged as they were. Each has a strong claim to be the original. They cannot both be, since one ship cannot be in two places. And it seems arbitrary to say that neither is.
paras.zh: 1655 年，霍布斯加了一個轉折，把一個古老的謎題變成了一個難題。假設有人把舊木板在拆下來的時候都留著，事後再照原來的次序把它們組起來。現在有兩艘船了。一艘停在港裡，就在特修斯之船一向停泊的地方，它是由原船經過逐步修補而來的。另一艘在倉庫裡，它恰恰是用特修斯航行時的那些木板、照原樣排列做成的。兩艘都有很強的理由自稱是原船。它們不可能都是，因為一艘船不可能在兩個地方。而說兩艘都不是，又似乎很武斷。

paras.en: Some care with words is needed first. Two coins from the same mint are the same in one sense, since they are exactly alike, and are plainly two coins. Philosophers call that qualitative identity. The puzzle concerns the other sense, numerical identity, being one and the same thing. The repaired ship and the original are certainly not alike in every respect. The question is whether they are one thing or two. Numerical identity obeys a strict logic. If A is the same thing as B, and B is the same thing as C, then A is the same thing as C. That is why Hobbes’s version hurts. If the ship in the harbor is the original, and the ship in the warehouse is the original, then the two are one ship, which is absurd.
paras.zh: 首先得在用詞上小心一點。同一個鑄幣廠出來的兩枚硬幣，在某個意義上是「一樣的」，因為它們一模一樣，但明明是兩枚硬幣。哲學家把那稱為「質的同一」。這個謎題關心的是另一個意思：「數的同一」，也就是「是同一個東西」。修補過的船與原船，肯定不是在每個方面都一樣。問題是：它們是一個東西，還是兩個？數的同一遵守嚴格的邏輯。如果 A 與 B 是同一個東西，B 與 C 是同一個東西，那麼 A 與 C 就是同一個東西。這就是霍布斯的版本讓人難受的原因：如果港裡的船是原船，倉庫裡的船也是原船，那麼這兩艘就是一艘船，而這是荒謬的。

paras.en: The first answer says that a thing is its matter. On this view the warehouse ship is the original, and the harbor ship is a new vessel that came into being plank by plank. Strictly applied, the view implies that nothing survives the loss of a single part, so that you are not the person who began reading this sentence. Few can live with that. The second answer says that a thing is its form and its continuous history. Aristotle held that what makes a ship a ship is its organization, and Locke made the same point about living things: “their identity depends not on a mass of the same particles, but on something else,” so that an oak is the same plant from seedling to great tree “as long as it partakes of the same life.” On this view the harbor ship wins.
paras.zh: 第一個答案說，一樣東西就是它的材料。照這個看法，倉庫裡的船才是原船，港裡的船是一塊木板一塊木板逐漸形成的新船。嚴格應用的話，這個看法蘊涵：任何東西只要失去一個部分，就不復存在；所以你已經不是開始讀這個句子的那個人了。很少有人受得了這個結論。第二個答案說，一樣東西就是它的形式與它連續的歷史。亞里斯多德主張，使船成為船的是它的組織結構；洛克對生物提出了同樣的論點：「它們的同一性不依賴於同一堆微粒，而是依賴於別的東西」，所以一棵橡樹從幼苗長成大樹，始終是同一株植物，「只要它分有同一個生命」。照這個看法，港裡的船贏了。

paras.en: The third answer changes the picture. Suppose a ship is extended in time as well as in space, a long four-dimensional thing of which each day’s ship is a slice. Then the question of which later ship is the earlier one was badly put. There are two overlapping histories that share their early stages and divide, as two roads may share a stretch of pavement. The fourth answer is the most deflating. It says that there is no further fact to discover. We know everything that happened to every plank. What remains is a decision about how to use the word “same,” and the decision properly depends on our purposes. A museum, an insurer, and a navy may each be right to count differently.
paras.zh: 第三個答案換了一幅圖像。假設一艘船除了在空間裡延展，也在時間裡延展，是一個長長的四維的東西，每一天的船只是它的一個切片。那麼「後來的哪一艘船是先前的那一艘」這個問題，本來就問得不好。有兩段重疊的歷史，它們共用早期的階段，然後分開，就像兩條路可以共用一段路面。第四個答案最洩氣。它說，沒有進一步的事實等著被發現。每一塊木板發生了什麼，我們全都知道。剩下的是一個決定：怎麼使用「同一」這個詞；而這個決定理當取決於我們的目的。博物館、保險公司與海軍，各自用不同的算法，可以都是對的。

paras.en: The puzzle is acted out in real institutions, and different cultures have settled it differently. At Ise in Japan, the principal shrine buildings are torn down and rebuilt on an adjoining plot every twenty years, in new cypress, to the same plan. This has been done more than sixty times since the seventh century. Nobody in Japan thinks that the shrine is twenty years old. Its identity is taken to lie in the form, the site, and the unbroken practice of the carpenters. European conservation long took the opposite view and prized original material above all, so that a restored cathedral was thought to have lost something a ruin kept. In 1994 an international meeting of conservators at Nara, prompted by cases like Ise, agreed that authenticity cannot be judged by one fixed standard and must be understood within each culture. The United States Navy keeps a wooden frigate of 1797, the Constitution, in commission, and only a small fraction of her timber is original. She is still the same ship in the eyes of the law.
paras.zh: 這個謎題在真實的制度裡不斷上演，而不同的文化用不同的方式解決它。在日本的伊勢，主要的神宮建築每二十年就拆掉，在相鄰的空地上用新的檜木、照同樣的規制重建。從七世紀以來，這已經做了六十多次。在日本，沒有人認為這座神宮只有二十年的歷史。它的同一性被認為在於形制、地點，以及匠人從未中斷的技藝傳承。歐洲的文物保存長期採取相反的看法，把原始材料看得高於一切，所以人們認為，一座修復過的大教堂失去了某種廢墟還保有的東西。1994 年，一場在奈良召開的國際文物保存會議，在伊勢這類案例的推動下，達成了共識：真實性不能用單一固定的標準來判斷，必須放在各個文化之內來理解。美國海軍讓一艘 1797 年的木造巡防艦「憲法號」保持現役，而她的木料只有一小部分是原件。在法律眼中，她仍然是同一艘船。

paras.en: The reason the puzzle has lasted is that it is about us. A human body exchanges matter with its surroundings continuously. Most of the atoms in it are replaced within a few years, though some cells, including most of the neurons in the cerebral cortex, last a lifetime. If matter were the standard of identity, the person who was promised something ten years ago would no longer exist to collect it, and the person who committed a crime could not be punished. We hold each other to promises and debts across decades, and so in practice we have all taken the side of form and continuity. Whether we are entitled to is the subject of later lessons on the self.
paras.zh: 這個謎題之所以流傳至今，是因為它談的就是我們。人的身體不斷地跟周遭交換物質。體內大部分的原子在幾年之內就被替換掉了，雖然有些細胞，包括大腦皮質裡大多數的神經元，會存續一輩子。如果材料是同一性的標準，那麼十年前被許下承諾的那個人，就不復存在、無從兌現了；犯了罪的那個人，也無法受罰。我們隔著幾十年，仍然要彼此對承諾與債務負責；所以在實踐上，我們全都站到了「形式與連續性」這一邊。至於我們有沒有資格這樣做，是後面談「自我」的幾課的主題。

paras.en: Zhuangzi has an image for the unease this causes. A man hides his boat in a ravine and thinks it safe, “yet at midnight a strong man carries it off on his back, and the sleeper knows nothing of it.” The strong man is change. One reading of the passage is that nothing stays hidden from it for even a night, and that the boat we find in the morning has already ceased to be the boat we hid.
paras.zh: 對於這件事引起的不安，莊子有一個意象。一個人把船藏在山谷裡，以為很牢靠，「然而夜半有力者負之而走，昧者不知也」。那個有力者就是變化。這段話的一種讀法是：沒有任何東西能躲開它，連一夜都躲不過；我們早上找到的那艘船，已經不是我們藏起來的那一艘了。

lab.title_zh: 親手做一次：把木板換掉
lab.lead_en: A 3D ship of seventy parts. Replace them one at a time, or let the years pass, and say when you think it stops being Theseus’s ship. When nothing original is left, rebuild the old planks on the shore and decide which of the two is his.
lab.lead_zh: 一艘由七十個零件組成的 3D 船。一次換一個，或者讓歲月自己過去；你覺得它在哪一刻不再是特修斯的船，就說出來。等到原件一塊不剩，把舊木板在岸上重組起來，再決定這兩艘哪一艘才是他的。

q.en: Two ships now exist. Which is the ship of Theseus?
q.zh: 現在有兩艘船。哪一艘是特修斯的船？

t.en: Ship A, repaired in the water
t.zh: 船 A，在水上修補的

opts.tag: Form and continuity · 形式與連續

r.en: You are with Aristotle and with Locke on living things: a thing is its organization and its unbroken history. The difficulty is ship B. Had the planks been removed all at once, cleaned, and reassembled, everyone would call the result the same ship. Why should doing it slowly, with a stand-in holding the place, make a difference?
r.zh: 你跟亞里斯多德站在一起，也跟談生物時的洛克站在一起：一樣東西就是它的組織結構與它未曾中斷的歷史。困難在船 B。假如那些木板是一次全部拆下、清理、再組回去，每個人都會說那是同一艘船。為什麼慢慢地做、中間有一個替身佔著位置，就會有差別？

t.en: Ship B, rebuilt from the old planks
t.zh: 船 B，用舊木板重組的

r.en: You hold that a thing is what it is made of. Then you must say when the ship in the water stopped being Theseus’s. If it was at the first plank, nothing survives any repair. If it was at some later plank, which one, and why that one?
r.zh: 你主張一樣東西就是構成它的材料。那麼你必須說出，水上那艘船是在什麼時候不再是特修斯的。如果是在換第一塊木板的時候，那麼任何東西都撐不過任何一次修補。如果是在後來的某一塊，是哪一塊？為什麼是那一塊？

t.en: Both of them
t.zh: 兩艘都是

r.en: One ship cannot be in two places, so read strictly this is a contradiction. It becomes coherent if a ship is a thing spread out in time. Then there are two ships, which shared all of their early stages and have now parted. The cost is that on the day Theseus sailed there were already two ships under him, exactly coinciding.
r.zh: 一艘船不可能在兩個地方，所以照字面讀，這是矛盾的。如果船是一個在時間中展開的東西，這個答案就說得通了：那麼有兩艘船，它們共用了全部的早期階段，現在分開了。代價是：特修斯航行的那一天，他腳下就已經有兩艘完全重合的船。

t.en: There is no fact of the matter
t.zh: 這件事沒有事實可言

r.en: You hold that once we know where every plank went, nothing is left to know, and “same ship” is a label we apply for our purposes. This dissolves the puzzle for ships. Ask yourself whether you are willing to say the same about a person, including yourself. Derek Parfit was. Most people find that they are not.
r.zh: 你主張：一旦我們知道每一塊木板去了哪裡，就沒有剩下什麼可知道的了；「同一艘船」是我們依自己的目的貼上去的標籤。這樣一來，船的謎題就化解了。問問你自己：對一個人，包括你自己，你願不願意說同樣的話？帕菲特願意。多數人發現自己不願意。

argument.lead_en: Hobbes’s version can be set out as an inconsistent set of claims, each of which is hard to give up. A solution has to say which one goes. Click a step to see what can be said against it.
argument.lead_zh: 霍布斯的版本可以攤開成一組互不相容的主張，每一個都很難放棄。一個解法必須說出該放棄哪一個。點任何一步，看看別人可以怎麼反對它。

steps.en: Replacing one plank of a ship does not destroy the ship. So the ship that has been gradually repaired is the original ship.
steps.zh: 換掉一艘船的一塊木板，並不會毀掉這艘船。所以，逐步修補過的那艘船就是原船。
steps.ob_en: Denied by those who hold that a thing is its matter. Notice that the step from “each replacement preserves the ship” to “all of them together do” has the shape of the heap paradox from lesson A4, and may fail for the same reason.
steps.ob_zh: 主張「東西就是它的材料」的人否認這一點。注意：從「每一次更換都保住了船」到「全部加起來也保住了船」這一步，形狀跟 A4 那一課的堆垛悖論一樣，可能基於同樣的理由而不成立。

steps.en: A ship that is taken apart and put together again from the same planks in the same arrangement is the same ship.
steps.zh: 一艘船被拆開，再用同樣的木板、照同樣的排列組回去，仍然是同一艘船。
steps.ob_en: Ordinary practice supports this: a tent, a watch, or a rifle survives being stripped and reassembled. One may add a condition, that nothing else has taken over the original’s role in the meantime. Critics ask why the existence of something elsewhere should decide what this thing is.
steps.ob_zh: 日常的做法支持這一點：帳篷、手錶、步槍，拆了再裝回去都還是原來那個。有人會加一個條件：在這期間，沒有別的東西接替了原物的角色。批評者問：為什麼「別處有另一樣東西存在」，可以決定「這樣東西是什麼」？

steps.en: The repaired ship and the reassembled ship are two ships, since they are in different places at the same time.
steps.zh: 修補過的船與重組的船是兩艘船，因為它們在同一個時間位於不同的地方。
steps.ob_en: Hardly deniable.
steps.ob_zh: 幾乎無法否認。

steps.en: Identity is transitive: if two things are each the same thing as a third, they are the same thing as each other.
steps.zh: 同一性有遞移性：如果兩樣東西各自都與第三樣東西同一，它們彼此就是同一的。
steps.ob_en: This is a law of logic, and almost no one gives it up. The four-dimensional view keeps it by redescribing the case: the two ships are never identical, and they only share parts.
steps.ob_zh: 這是一條邏輯定律，幾乎沒有人會放棄它。四維的看法保住了它，方法是重新描述這個情況：兩艘船從來不是同一的，它們只是共用了一些部分。

steps.en: These four cannot all be true. From the first two, each ship is the original. By the fourth they are then one ship, which the third denies.
steps.zh: 這四個不可能全部為真。由前兩個，兩艘船各自都是原船。依第四個，它們就是一艘船，而這是第三個所否認的。
steps.ob_en: Most philosophers reject the first or the second premise, and they disagree about which. That disagreement tracks a real difference of temperament, between those who think of a thing as its stuff and those who think of it as a pattern that stuff passes through.
steps.ob_zh: 多數哲學家否定第一個或第二個前提，而對於否定哪一個，他們意見不一。這個分歧反映了一種真實的氣質差異：有些人把一樣東西想成它的材料，有些人把它想成材料流經的一個樣式。

source.work: Plutarch, Life of Theseus 23; Saṃyutta Nikāya 5.10
source.work_zh: 普魯塔克《特修斯傳》第 23 節；《相應部》5.10
source.tr: Plutarch in the Dryden translation revised by A. H. Clough (public domain); the Pāli verse in our own translation
source.lead_en: The Greek source for the puzzle is a single sentence in a biography. An Indian text of similar age asks the same question about a chariot and gives a definite answer.
source.lead_zh: 這個謎題的希臘文出處，是一部傳記裡的一個句子。一部年代相近的印度文獻，對一輛車問了同樣的問題，並且給了明確的答案。

passages.en: …they took away the old planks as they decayed, putting in new and stronger timber in their place, insomuch that this ship became a standing example among the philosophers, for the logical question as to things that grow; one side holding that the ship remained the same, and the other contending that it was not the same.
passages.zh: ……舊木板一朽壞，他們就拆掉，換上新的、更堅固的木料；以致於這艘船在哲學家當中成了一個現成的例子，用來討論關於「會生長的東西」的邏輯問題：一方主張船還是同一艘，另一方堅稱它已經不是同一艘了。
passages.note_en: The phrase “things that grow” shows what the philosophers were really arguing about. The Growing Argument was an old puzzle about living things: if a creature is its matter, then whenever it takes in food it becomes a different creature, and nobody ever grows. The ship was useful because it changes slowly and in plain view. Plutarch does not tell us who was right, and he does not seem to think he needs to. (“Insomuch that” means “to such a degree that.”)
passages.note_zh: 「會生長的東西」這個詞組，顯示了哲學家們真正在爭的是什麼。「生長論證」是一個關於生物的古老謎題：如果一個生物就是它的材料，那麼每當牠攝取食物，牠就成了另一個生物，結果是沒有誰曾經長大。這艘船之所以好用，是因為它變得慢，而且變化看得見。普魯塔克沒有告訴我們誰對，他似乎也不覺得有這個必要。（insomuch that 的意思是「到了……的程度」。）

passages.en: Just as, when the parts are assembled, there is the word “chariot,” so, when the aggregates are present, there is the convention “a being.”
passages.zh: 譬如眾分和合，而有「車」這個名稱；同樣地，諸蘊存在時，就有「眾生」這個世俗的說法。
passages.note_en: The Pāli is: yathā hi aṅgasambhārā, hoti saddo ratho iti; evaṃ khandhesu santesu, hoti sattoti sammuti. Two words carry the doctrine. Sadda, “word,” says that “chariot” is a name applied to assembled parts. Sammuti, “convention,” says the same of a living being. This is the fourth answer above, stated some two thousand years before Hobbes and applied without hesitation to persons. The monk Nāgasena later used the same chariot to instruct the Greek king Milinda.
passages.note_zh: 巴利原文是：yathā hi aṅgasambhārā, hoti saddo ratho iti; evaṃ khandhesu santesu, hoti sattoti sammuti。有兩個詞承載了這個教義。sadda，「名稱」，說的是「車」只是加在組合起來的零件上的一個名字。sammuti，「世俗、約定」，對有情眾生說了同樣的話。這就是上面的第四個答案；它比霍布斯早了大約兩千年就被提出來，並且毫不猶豫地用在人身上。後來那先比丘用同一輛車，來教導希臘裔的彌蘭王。

items.o_en: This is a dispute about a word. Once we know what happened to each plank, there is nothing left to argue about, and people who go on arguing are confused.
items.o_zh: 這是一場關於字詞的爭論。一旦我們知道每一塊木板發生了什麼，就沒有什麼可爭的了；還在爭的人是搞糊塗了。
items.r_en: For a ship this may be right, and it is the fourth answer. But identity has consequences that words do not. Who owns the vessel, who is liable for its debts, whether a promise made to its captain still binds: these depend on which ship is which. And when the same reasoning is turned on persons, the conventionalist must say that whether I will exist tomorrow is a matter of how we choose to speak. Some accept that. It is not a trivial thing to accept.
items.r_zh: 對一艘船來說，這也許是對的，而它就是第四個答案。但同一性有字詞所沒有的後果。這艘船歸誰所有、誰要為它的債務負責、對它的船長許下的承諾是否仍然有約束力：這些都取決於哪一艘是哪一艘。而當同樣的推理轉到人身上時，約定論者就必須說：我明天存不存在，取決於我們選擇怎麼說話。有人接受這一點。接受它並不是一件輕鬆的事。

items.o_en: The puzzle arises only for artifacts. Living things and persons have a real principle of unity, a life or a mind, and so it does not touch them.
items.o_zh: 這個謎題只發生在人造物上。生物與人有真正的統一原則——一個生命，或一個心靈——所以它碰不到他們。
items.r_en: Locke thought so about organisms, and it is true that nobody collects a creature’s discarded cells and builds a rival from them. But the division of an amoeba, or the imagined case of a brain whose two halves are transplanted into two bodies, reproduces Hobbes’s structure exactly: one original, two continuers, each with a good claim. The puzzle follows wherever a thing can have two successors.
items.r_zh: 洛克對生物體是這麼想的；而且確實沒有人會去蒐集一個生物丟棄的細胞，用它們造出一個對手。但是一隻變形蟲的分裂，或者想像中「一個腦的兩半被分別移植到兩個身體」的情況，把霍布斯的結構原封不動地重現了：一個原物，兩個延續者，各自都有很好的理由。一樣東西只要可能有兩個後繼者，這個謎題就跟到哪裡。

items.o_en: If nothing is strictly the same from one moment to the next, responsibility collapses. No one could be blamed, thanked, or held to a contract.
items.o_zh: 如果沒有任何東西從一個時刻到下一個時刻嚴格地保持同一，責任就崩潰了。沒有人可以被責備、被感謝，或被要求履行契約。
items.r_en: This does not follow. Responsibility needs a relation between the earlier agent and the later one that is close enough and of the right kind: continuity of memory, character, and intention. It does not need an unchanging core. We already work this way, holding people more or less responsible as they are more or less connected to what they did. Whether continuity without identity is really enough is argued in lesson A13.
items.r_zh: 這推不出來。責任需要的是先前的行為者與後來的行為者之間，有一種夠緊密、而且種類正確的關係：記憶、性格與意圖的連續。它並不需要一個不變的核心。我們本來就是這樣運作的：一個人跟他做過的事連結得多或少，我們就要他負多或少的責任。至於「有連續而沒有同一」是不是真的夠，留到 A13 那一課討論。

said.claim: Every cell in your body is replaced every seven years.
said.claim_zh: 你身體裡的每一個細胞，每七年就全部換過一輪。
said.en: This is the fact most often quoted alongside the Ship of Theseus, and it is false. Turnover varies enormously. Cells lining the gut last a few days and red blood cells about four months. Carbon dating of human tissue, published in 2005, showed that most neurons of the cerebral cortex are as old as the person, as are the cells at the center of the lens of the eye. The atoms within long-lived cells are exchanged all the same, so the puzzle survives the correction.
said.zh: 這是最常跟特修斯之船一起被引用的「事實」，而它是錯的。汰換的速度差別極大。腸道內壁的細胞只活幾天，紅血球大約四個月。2005 年發表的人體組織碳定年研究顯示，大腦皮質的大多數神經元跟這個人本身一樣老，眼睛水晶體中央的細胞也是。不過，長壽細胞內的原子照樣在更換，所以這個謎題並沒有因為這項更正而消失。

terms.o: Gk. ta meta ta physika ‘the books after the Physics’
terms.d_en: The study of what exists and of its most general features: identity, change, time, cause.
terms.d_zh: 研究什麼存在、以及存在物最普遍的特徵：同一、變化、時間、因果。

terms.d_en: Being one and the same thing.
terms.d_zh: 是同一個東西。

terms.d_en: Being exactly alike, as two copies of a book are.
terms.d_zh: 一模一樣，就像同一本書的兩本。

terms.d_en: A thing’s continuing to exist through time and change.
terms.d_zh: 一樣東西經歷時間與變化而繼續存在。

terms.d_en: The theory of parts and wholes.
terms.d_zh: 關於部分與整體的理論。

terms.d_en: The property of a relation such that if it holds from A to B and from B to C, it holds from A to C.
terms.d_zh: 關係的一種性質：如果它在 A 與 B 之間成立，在 B 與 C 之間也成立，它就在 A 與 C 之間成立。

terms.d_en: The view that objects are extended in time and have temporal parts, as they have spatial parts.
terms.d_zh: 主張物體在時間中延展，有時間上的部分，就像有空間上的部分一樣。

terms.d_en: Here, the view that questions of identity are settled by our decisions about how to speak.
terms.d_zh: 在這裡指：同一性的問題，由我們「怎麼說話」的決定來解決。

vocab.eg: They replaced the timber, insomuch that the ship became a standing example.
vocab.eg_zh: 他們更換木料，以致於這艘船成了一個現成的例子。

vocab.eg: Both sides have a case.
vocab.eg_zh: 雙方都有道理。

vocab.eg: Not one splinter that Theseus touched is left.
vocab.eg_zh: 特修斯碰過的木頭，連一根碎片都不剩。

vocab.eg: A replica is a different thing from the original.
vocab.eg_zh: 複製品跟原物是兩樣東西。

vocab.eg: Hobbes added a twist that turned an old puzzle into a hard one.
vocab.eg_zh: 霍布斯加了一個轉折，把古老的謎題變成難題。

vocab.eg: It seems arbitrary to say that neither is the original.
vocab.eg_zh: 說兩艘都不是原船，似乎很武斷。

vocab.eg: Few can live with that conclusion.
vocab.eg_zh: 很少有人受得了那個結論。

vocab.eg: The fourth answer is the most deflating.
vocab.eg_zh: 第四個答案最洩氣。

vocab.eg: The puzzle is acted out in real institutions.
vocab.eg_zh: 這個謎題在真實的制度裡不斷上演。

vocab.eg: We hold each other to promises across decades.
vocab.eg_zh: 我們隔著幾十年，仍然要彼此對承諾負責。

quiz.q: What is the difference between numerical and qualitative identity?
options: Being one and the same thing, as against being exactly alike.
Being counted, as against being weighed.
Being old, as against being new.
There is no difference.

quiz.q: What does Hobbes’s addition to the puzzle introduce?
options: A second ship, rebuilt from the original planks.
A storm that sinks the ship.
A dispute about who owned the ship.
A second Theseus.

quiz.q: On the view that a thing is its matter, which is the ship of Theseus?
options: The one reassembled from the old planks.
The one that was repaired in the harbor.
Both of them.
Whichever is larger.

quiz.q: What does the rebuilding of the Ise shrine illustrate?
options: A culture can locate identity in form, site, and practice, and not in original material.
Wooden buildings cannot last twenty years.
Japan has no old buildings.
Shrines are always replicas.

quiz.q: According to the nun Vajirā’s verse, what is a “chariot”?
options: A word applied when the parts are assembled.
A substance underlying the parts.
The axle alone.
An illusion with no parts.

write.en: Choose an object you own that has been repaired or partly replaced over the years: a bicycle, a house, a pair of shoes. Is it the same one? Say which standard you are using.
write.zh: 選一樣你擁有、多年來修過或部分換過的東西：腳踏車、房子、一雙鞋。它還是同一個嗎？說出你用的是哪一種標準。

write.en: Which of the four answers did you choose in the exercise, and what would you say to someone who chose a different one? About 150 words.
write.zh: 在練習裡，你選了四個答案中的哪一個？對選了別的答案的人，你會說什麼？大約 150 個英文字。

write.en: An organization you belong to has changed all its members since it was founded. In what sense is it the same organization? Does your answer differ from your answer about the ship?
write.zh: 你所屬的某個組織，從創立到現在，成員已經全部換過。它在什麼意義上還是同一個組織？你的答案跟你對那艘船的答案一樣嗎？

paras.en: Buddhist philosophers met this puzzle early and took a clear position on it. In The Questions of King Milinda, the monk Nāgasena asks the king how he came, and the king says by chariot. Is the pole the chariot? The axle? The wheels? Is it all of them heaped together? Is it something apart from them? To each the king must answer no. “Chariot,” Nāgasena concludes, is a designation in common use, applied in dependence on the parts, and “Nāgasena” is a designation of the same kind, applied in dependence on a body, feelings, perceptions, volitions, and consciousness. No separate thing answers to either name.
paras.zh: 佛教哲學家很早就遇上了這個謎題，並且對它採取了明確的立場。在《彌蘭王問經》裡，那先比丘問國王是怎麼來的，國王說坐車來的。那麼，轅是車嗎？軸是車嗎？輪是車嗎？是它們全部堆在一起嗎？還是在它們之外另有一個東西？每一問，國王都只能答「不是」。那先的結論是：「車」是一個通用的名稱，依於這些零件而施設；「那先」也是同一類的名稱，依於色、受、想、行、識而施設。這兩個名字，都沒有一個獨立的東西與之對應。

paras.en: This is the fourth answer, conventionalism, and Buddhism accepts the consequence that Western conventionalists often resist: it applies to me. The tradition distinguishes two levels. Conventionally there are ships, chariots, and persons, and it is true to say that this is the shrine founded thirteen centuries ago. Ultimately there are only the parts and their relations, arising and passing in dependence on one another. Abhidharma philosophers went further and held that the parts themselves last only a moment, so that every thing is a ship of Theseus whose planks are replaced continuously. Asked whether the one reborn is the same as the one who died, Nāgasena gives the answer that fits the ship as well: neither the same nor another (na ca so na ca añño). He compares it to a flame that burns through the night. It is one fire in the ordinary sense, though no part of it lasts (Dharma and the West, D2 and D16).
paras.zh: 這就是第四個答案，約定論；而佛教接受了西方的約定論者常常抗拒的那個後果：它適用於「我」。這個傳統區分兩個層次。就世俗而言，有船、有車、有人；說「這就是一千三百年前創建的那座神宮」，是真的。就勝義而言，只有那些部分以及它們之間的關係，彼此依待著生起、滅去。阿毘達磨的哲學家走得更遠，主張連那些部分本身也只存續一剎那；所以每一樣東西都是一艘特修斯之船，它的木板不斷地在更換。有人問：再生的那個人，跟死去的那個人是同一個嗎？那先給的答案，用在那艘船上也一樣貼切：「非一亦非異」（na ca so na ca añño）。他拿燒了一整夜的火焰來比喻：就平常的意思說，那是同一把火，雖然它沒有任何一部分是持續的（佛法與西方哲學 D2、D16）。
