philosophers.name: Socrates
philosophers.tag_en: The man who wrote nothing and changed what philosophy is about.
philosophers.tag_zh: 一個字也沒寫，卻改變了哲學在問什麼的人。
facts: Sophroniscus, a stoneworker; Phaenarete, a midwife

paras.en: Socrates was born around 470 BCE, when Athens was becoming the richest and most confident city in Greece. His father, Sophroniscus, is said to have worked in stone; his mother, Phaenarete, was a midwife, a fact Plato later turned into a metaphor. He was not rich and not handsome. His friends compared him to a satyr: snub nose, bulging eyes, the same old cloak in every season, and no shoes.
paras.zh: 蘇格拉底大約生於西元前 470 年，當時雅典正要成為希臘最富有、最有自信的城邦。據說他的父親索弗羅尼斯科斯是石匠；母親費納瑞特是接生婆，這件事後來被柏拉圖變成一個比喻。他不富有，也不好看。朋友拿他比作森林裡的薩提爾：塌鼻、凸眼，一年四季同一件舊斗篷，而且不穿鞋。

paras.en: He served as a heavy infantryman in three campaigns of the long war with Sparta, at Potidaea, Delium, and Amphipolis. The young aristocrat Alcibiades, whose life he saved at Potidaea, reported that Socrates endured cold and hunger better than anyone and walked off the lost field at Delium so calmly that no enemy cared to approach him.
paras.zh: 在對斯巴達的長年戰爭中，他以重裝步兵的身分參加過三場戰役：波提狄亞、德里昂、安菲波利斯。年輕貴族阿爾基比亞德在波提狄亞被他救過一命；據他說，蘇格拉底比誰都耐寒耐餓，而德里昂兵敗撤退時，他走得那樣從容，敵人沒有一個想靠近。

paras.en: At his trial Socrates explained how his odd career began. His friend Chaerephon had asked the oracle at Delphi whether anyone was wiser than Socrates, and the priestess had answered that no one was. Socrates, aware of having “no wisdom, small or great,” set out to refute the god by finding a wiser man. He questioned politicians, poets, and craftsmen, and found that each believed he knew things he did not. He concluded that the oracle meant something modest: he was wiser only in not mistaking his ignorance for knowledge.
paras.zh: 蘇格拉底在法庭上解釋過，他那古怪的生涯是怎麼開始的。他的朋友凱勒豐去德爾菲問神諭：有沒有人比蘇格拉底更有智慧？女祭司回答說沒有。蘇格拉底自知「大小智慧都沒有」，就動身去找一個更有智慧的人，想藉此反駁神。他問過政治家、詩人、工匠，發現每一個都以為自己知道一些其實不知道的事。他的結論是，神諭的意思很平實：他比較有智慧，只在於他沒有把自己的無知誤認為知識。

paras.en: From then on he spent his days in the agora and the gymnasia, questioning anyone who would stop. He charged no fee, which set him apart from the professional teachers called sophists, and he denied that he taught anything at all. He compared himself to a gadfly sent to sting a large and sluggish horse, and to a midwife who helps others deliver ideas while having none of her own.
paras.zh: 從那以後，他整天待在市集與體育場，逢人就問，只要對方肯停下來。他不收學費，這一點使他跟那些稱為「智者」的職業教師不同；他甚至否認自己教過任何東西。他把自己比作一隻牛虻，被派來叮一匹龐大而遲鈍的馬；又比作接生婆，幫別人把想法生出來，自己卻沒有孩子。

paras.en: Athens lost the war in 404 BCE and endured a brutal oligarchy, the Thirty, several of whose leaders had once kept company with Socrates. Socrates himself had defied them: ordered to arrest an innocent man, Leon of Salamis, he simply went home. Democracy was restored the next year, and in 399 three citizens, Meletus, Anytus, and Lycon, brought him to court. The charge, in Plato’s wording, was that he “corrupts the youth” and “does not believe in the gods of the state, but has other new divinities of his own.”
paras.zh: 西元前 404 年雅典戰敗，接著經歷了殘暴的寡頭統治「三十人僭主」，其中幾位領袖從前跟蘇格拉底來往過。蘇格拉底自己倒是違抗過他們：他們命令他去逮捕一個無辜的人，薩拉米斯的勒翁，他直接回家了。第二年民主政體恢復；西元前 399 年，美勒托斯、安尼托斯、呂孔三位公民把他告上法庭。照柏拉圖的記載，罪名是他「敗壞青年」，並且「不信城邦所信的神，另立自己的新神」。

paras.en: A jury of several hundred citizens found him guilty by a narrow margin; had thirty votes gone the other way, he says, he would have been acquitted. Asked to propose his own penalty, he suggested free meals at public expense, then a small fine. The jury chose death. He refused a chance to escape, arguing that a citizen who has accepted the laws all his life may not break them when they turn against him, and a month later he drank the hemlock among his friends. In Plato’s account his last words were a reminder to pay a debt: “Crito, we owe a cock to Asclepius.”
paras.zh: 由數百位公民組成的陪審團以些微差距判他有罪；他說，只要有三十票投向另一邊，他就無罪了。輪到他自己提議刑罰時，他先提議由公家供他免費用餐，後來才改口說可以繳一筆小額罰金。陪審團選了死刑。他拒絕了逃亡的機會，理由是：一個公民一輩子都接受法律，就不能在法律轉而對他不利的時候違反它。一個月後，他在朋友圍繞之下喝了毒芹汁。照柏拉圖的記述，他最後一句話是提醒朋友還一筆債：「克里托，我們還欠阿斯克勒庇俄斯一隻公雞。」

timeline: Mocked on stage in Aristophanes’ Clouds
阿里斯托芬在喜劇《雲》裡嘲弄他
Refuses to put an illegal motion to the vote
拒絕把違法的動議付諸表決

idea.title_en: The central idea: knowing what you do not know
idea.title_zh: 核心觀念：知道自己不知道

paras.en: Before Socrates, Greek thinkers had mostly asked what the world is made of. Socrates asked how to live, and he asked it in a new way. He assumed that anyone who is good at something can say what he is doing. A doctor can explain health; a brave man ought to be able to explain courage. When the explanation collapses under questioning, the person’s confidence has been shown to rest on nothing, and the search can start.
paras.zh: 在蘇格拉底之前，希臘思想家問的多半是世界由什麼構成。蘇格拉底問的是人該怎麼活，而且用一種新的方式問。他假定：一個人真的擅長一件事，就說得出自己在做什麼。醫生能解釋健康；勇敢的人應該能解釋勇敢。當這個解釋在追問之下垮掉，就表示這個人的自信沒有根據，而尋找可以開始了。

paras.en: Behind the method lies a bold thesis, usually called Socratic intellectualism: virtue is a kind of knowledge. If you really knew what was good for you, you would do it; so no one does wrong willingly, and all wrongdoing is a form of ignorance. That is why examining beliefs was, for him, a moral task and not an academic one.
paras.zh: 這套方法背後有一個大膽的主張，通常稱為蘇格拉底的「主知主義」：德行是一種知識。如果你真的知道什麼對自己是好的，你就會去做；所以沒有人是自願作惡的，一切過錯都是某種無知。這就是為什麼對他來說，省察信念是道德的工作，不是學院的工作。

quote.en: …the unexamined life is not worth living…
quote.note_en: Spoken after the guilty verdict, to explain why he would not accept exile on condition of silence.
quote.note_zh: 說於有罪判決之後，用來解釋他為什麼不接受「閉嘴就可以流亡」的條件。

objection.title_en: The strongest objection: weakness of will

paras.en: If virtue is knowledge, it should be impossible to know what is best and do otherwise. Yet this seems to happen every day: the smoker knows, the procrastinator knows. The Greeks called it akrasia, lack of self-mastery. Aristotle, who admired Socrates, said bluntly that the Socratic view is at odds with what we plainly observe (Nicomachean Ethics VII.2).
paras.zh: 如果德行就是知識，那麼「明知什麼最好卻不去做」應該是不可能的。可是這種事似乎天天發生：抽菸的人知道，拖延的人也知道。希臘人稱之為 akrasia，缺乏自制。亞里斯多德很敬佩蘇格拉底，卻直截了當地說，蘇格拉底的看法跟我們明明看到的事實不合（《尼各馬可倫理學》卷七第二章）。

paras.en: A Socratic can reply that the smoker does not fully know: at the moment of choice the nearer pleasure looks larger than it is, the way a nearby object looks bigger than a distant one, and what he lacks is an art of measuring (Protagoras 356c–357b). Whether that reply rescues the thesis or merely redefines “knowledge” is still disputed.
paras.zh: 蘇格拉底這一邊可以回答：抽菸的人並不是「完全知道」。在選擇的當下，近處的快樂看起來比實際大，就像近的東西看起來比遠的大；他缺的是一門「衡量的技藝」（《普羅塔哥拉篇》356c–357b）。這個回答究竟救回了原來的主張，還是只是把「知識」重新定義了一次，至今仍有爭論。

paras.en: Because Socrates wrote nothing, everything we know comes through others, and they do not agree. Aristophanes, writing while Socrates was alive, shows a ridiculous charlatan in a basket. Xenophon shows a sensible moral adviser. Plato shows a philosophical genius, and he keeps using “Socrates” as a character for decades, long after the views expressed have become Plato’s own. Scholars usually treat the early, short dialogues that end in aporia (Apology, Euthyphro, Laches) as closest to the historical man, and admit that this is a judgment and not a certainty.
paras.zh: 因為蘇格拉底什麼都沒寫，我們知道的一切都是經由別人，而這些人的說法並不一致。阿里斯托芬在蘇格拉底還活著的時候寫劇本，劇中的他是個吊在籃子裡的可笑騙子。色諾芬筆下的他，是個通情達理的道德顧問。柏拉圖筆下的他是哲學天才；而且柏拉圖把「蘇格拉底」這個角色用了幾十年，用到後來，角色口中的見解早已是柏拉圖自己的。學者通常把早期那些以困惑收場的短篇對話錄（《申辯篇》《歐緒弗洛篇》《拉凱斯篇》）視為最接近歷史上的那個人，同時也承認這是一種判斷，不是定論。

said.claim: “The only true wisdom is in knowing you know nothing.”
said.claim_zh: 「唯一真正的智慧，是知道自己一無所知。」
said.en: No ancient source has Socrates say this. It paraphrases Apology 21d and 23a–b, where he interprets the oracle to mean that human wisdom is worth little, and that the wisest person is the one who, like Socrates, recognizes this.
said.zh: 沒有任何古代文獻記載蘇格拉底說過這句話。它是《申辯篇》21d 與 23a–b 的改寫；在那裡，他把神諭解釋為：人的智慧沒什麼價值，而最有智慧的，是像蘇格拉底這樣看出這一點的人。

paras.en: The two were near contemporaries and never heard of each other. Both wrote nothing, taught by conversation, took no fee, and were remembered through dialogues composed by followers. Both held that the root of going wrong is a kind of ignorance: for Socrates, not knowing what is good; for the Buddha, avijjā, not seeing things as they are.
paras.zh: 這兩個人的年代相去不遠，彼此從未聽過對方。兩人都沒有著作，都用談話教人，都不收費，也都靠弟子編寫的對話被後人記得。兩人都認為，人走錯路的根源是某種無知：在蘇格拉底是不知道什麼是善；在佛陀是無明（avijjā），沒有如實看見事物。

paras.en: The difference shows in the remedy. For Socrates the cure is argument, and he seems to think that seeing the truth is enough to act on it. The Buddhist path adds training of attention and conduct, on the view that craving does not dissolve merely because one has reached a correct conclusion. That is, in effect, a Buddhist answer to the problem of akrasia.
paras.zh: 差別在藥方。蘇格拉底的藥是論證，而且他似乎認為，看見了真理就足以照著去做。佛教的道路多了對注意力與行為的訓練（戒與定），因為它認為，貪愛不會只因為人得出了正確的結論就消散。這其實就是佛教對「意志薄弱」問題的回答。

terms.d_en: A paid traveling teacher of rhetoric and public skill in fifth-century Greece.
terms.d_zh: 西元前五世紀希臘收費授課、教授修辭與公共事務能力的巡迴教師。

terms.d_en: His habit of professing ignorance and praising the other speaker’s expertise before testing it.
terms.d_zh: 他在檢驗對方之前，先自稱無知、稱讚對方內行的習慣。

terms.d_en: Describing teaching that draws ideas out of the learner by questions (Theaetetus 149a–151d).
terms.d_zh: 形容用提問把想法從學習者身上引出來的教法（《泰阿泰德篇》149a–151d）。

terms.d_en: Acting against one’s own better judgment.
terms.d_zh: 違背自己較好的判斷去行動。

terms.d_en: The inner sign Socrates said warned him against certain actions; it only ever said no.
terms.d_zh: 蘇格拉底說會警告他別做某些事的內在徵兆；它只會說「不」。

terms.d_en: The difficulty of recovering the historical Socrates from conflicting sources.
terms.d_zh: 從彼此衝突的史料中還原歷史上的蘇格拉底，這件事的困難。

quiz.q: How did Socrates interpret the oracle’s statement that no one was wiser than he?
options: He alone did not mistake his ignorance for knowledge.
He possessed secret knowledge from the gods.
The oracle had been bribed by Chaerephon.
Wisdom cannot be found in Athens.

quiz.q: What does “Socratic intellectualism” claim?
options: Virtue is a kind of knowledge, so no one does wrong willingly.
Only intellectuals can be virtuous.
Knowledge is impossible.
Virtue cannot be defined.

quiz.q: Why is it hard to know what the historical Socrates thought?
options: He wrote nothing, and the surviving portraits disagree.
His books were burned after the trial.
Plato never mentions him.
He taught only in secret.

philosophers.name: Aristotle
philosophers.tag_en: He divided knowledge into the subjects we still study, and invented the science that checks reasoning in all of them.
philosophers.tag_zh: 他把知識分成我們至今還在讀的科目，並且發明了檢查一切科目推理的那門學問。
facts: 322 BCE, Chalcis, on the island of Euboea
Nicomachus, physician to the king of Macedon

paras.en: Aristotle was born in 384 BCE at Stagira, a small town in the north of Greece. His father, Nicomachus, was physician to the king of Macedon, and it is tempting to see the doctor’s son in the philosopher who later dissected cuttlefish and classified some five hundred kinds of animal. Orphaned young, he was sent at seventeen to Athens to study at Plato’s Academy, and he stayed for about twenty years, until Plato died.
paras.zh: 亞里斯多德西元前 384 年生於希臘北部的小鎮斯塔基拉。父親尼各馬可是馬其頓國王的御醫；這位哲學家日後解剖烏賊、替大約五百種動物分類，讓人很難不在他身上看到醫生兒子的影子。他年少失怙，十七歲被送到雅典，進柏拉圖的學院求學，一待大約二十年，直到柏拉圖去世。

paras.en: He was never a citizen of Athens and could not own property there. He was also never simply a disciple. Where Plato looked past the changing world to eternal Forms, Aristotle came to hold that the form of a thing is found in the thing, and that knowledge begins from careful observation of particulars. A later saying sums up his attitude: Plato is dear to me, but truth is dearer. The wording is medieval; the thought is his (Nicomachean Ethics I.6).
paras.zh: 他始終不是雅典公民，在那裡不能擁有產業。他也從來不只是個門徒。柏拉圖把目光越過變動的世界，望向永恆的「理型」；亞里斯多德後來則主張，事物的形式就在事物之中，知識要從仔細觀察個別事物開始。後世有句話概括了他的態度：「吾愛吾師，吾更愛真理。」這個措辭是中世紀的，意思卻是他自己的（《尼各馬可倫理學》卷一第六章）。

paras.en: When Plato died in 347, Aristotle left Athens. He spent several years on the coast of Asia Minor and on the island of Lesbos, where, with his friend Theophrastus, he did much of the biological research that fills a quarter of his surviving work. Around 343 Philip of Macedon invited him to tutor his thirteen-year-old son, the future Alexander the Great. What the philosopher taught the conqueror, and how much of it stayed, nobody knows.
paras.zh: 西元前 347 年柏拉圖去世，亞里斯多德離開雅典。他在小亞細亞沿岸與列斯伏斯島住了幾年；他現存著作有四分之一是生物學，其中大部分的研究，就是在那裡跟朋友泰奧弗拉斯托斯一起做的。大約西元前 343 年，馬其頓的腓力請他去教自己十三歲的兒子，也就是日後的亞歷山大大帝。哲學家教了征服者什麼、留下了多少，沒有人知道。

paras.en: In 335 he returned to Athens and opened his own school in a public gymnasium called the Lyceum. Its members were nicknamed Peripatetics, probably from the covered walk, the peripatos, where they talked. The Lyceum was something new: a research institute, with a library, collections of specimens, and teams compiling the constitutions of 158 Greek cities.
paras.zh: 西元前 335 年他回到雅典，在一座名叫呂克昂的公共體育場開了自己的學校。學校的成員被稱為「逍遙學派」，這個綽號大概來自他們邊走邊談的那條有頂走廊（peripatos）。呂克昂是一種新的東西：一所研究機構，有圖書館、有標本收藏，還有團隊在彙編 158 個希臘城邦的政制。

paras.en: What survives from those years is about thirty treatises, roughly a third of what he wrote. They are not polished books. They read like lecture notes, dense and abrupt, and the dialogues he published for the public, which Cicero praised as a golden river of eloquence, are lost. When Alexander died in 323, Athens turned on everything Macedonian, and a charge of impiety was prepared against Aristotle. He withdrew to Chalcis, reportedly saying that he would not let the Athenians sin twice against philosophy, and died there the following year.
paras.zh: 那些年留下來的是大約三十部專論，約佔他全部著作的三分之一。它們不是精心修飾的書，讀起來像講課筆記，濃縮而突兀；他為一般讀者發表的對話錄，西塞羅曾讚美為「雄辯的金色河流」，卻全都失傳了。西元前 323 年亞歷山大去世，雅典轉而敵視一切跟馬其頓有關的東西，有人準備以「不敬神」的罪名控告亞里斯多德。他退居卡爾基斯，據說留下一句話：他不讓雅典人對哲學犯第二次罪。第二年他在那裡去世。

timeline: 亞歷山大去世；被控不敬神

idea.title_en: The central idea: Reasoning has a form
idea.title_zh: 核心觀念：推理有它的形式

paras.en: Aristotle’s logical works were later bundled under the title Organon, “the tool,” and the name is exact. He did not regard logic as one science among others. It was the instrument every science uses. His discovery was that whether a conclusion follows depends on the arrangement of terms in an argument and not on what the terms mean, so that arrangements can be studied systematically. In the Prior Analytics he worked through every combination of two premises of four kinds, identified those that yield a conclusion of necessity, and showed how the rest reduce to a few basic patterns. No one had attempted anything like it. Near the end of the Organon he says so himself: on this subject there was nothing at all before him to build on.
paras.zh: 亞里斯多德的邏輯著作後來被合編在《工具論》（Organon）這個標題下，這個名字很精確。他不把邏輯看成眾多科學當中的一門；它是每一門科學都要用的工具。他的發現是：結論推不推得出來，取決於論證裡詞項的排列，而不是詞項的意思，所以排列方式可以有系統地研究。在《前分析篇》裡，他把四種命題兩兩組合成前提的每一種情形都走過一遍，辨認出哪些必然得出結論，並證明其餘的可以化約為少數幾個基本樣式。在他之前沒有人做過類似的事。《工具論》接近結尾處，他自己也這麼說：在這個題目上，他之前完全沒有可以憑藉的東西。

paras.en: The same habit of mind runs through everything else he touched. To understand a thing is to grasp its causes, and he distinguished four: what it is made of, what form it has, what brought it about, and what it is for. To live well is to exercise, over a whole life, the excellences proper to a human being, which is what he meant by eudaimonia. To be good at feeling and acting is to hit the mean between too much and too little, as courage lies between cowardice and rashness. In each field he begins by collecting the opinions of “the many and the wise,” sorts out the puzzles, and builds from there.
paras.zh: 同一種思考習慣貫穿他碰過的一切。了解一樣東西，就是掌握它的原因；他分出四種：它由什麼構成、有什麼形式、由什麼促成、為了什麼目的。活得好，就是在一整個人生中發揮人之為人所特有的卓越，這是他說的 eudaimonia（幸福、人的興盛）。在感受與行動上做得好，就是命中太多與太少之間的「中道」，就像勇敢位於懦弱與魯莽之間。在每個領域，他都先蒐集「多數人與有智慧的人」的意見，理清其中的疑難，再從那裡往上蓋。

quote.en: All men by nature desire to know.
quote.ref: Aristotle, Metaphysics I.1, 980a, tr. W. D. Ross
quote.note_en: The first sentence of the Metaphysics. His evidence is that we enjoy seeing things even when it is of no use to us.
quote.note_zh: 《形上學》的第一句。他的證據是：即使沒有用處，我們也喜歡看東西。

objection.title_en: The strongest objection: The logic was too small
objection.title_zh: 最強的反駁：這套邏輯太小了

paras.en: For two thousand years Aristotle’s logic was treated as finished. Kant wrote in 1787 that since Aristotle logic had not needed to retrace a single step, and had not been able to advance one either. Less than a century later it was shown to be a fragment. The syllogism handles statements built from two terms, “all A are B.” It cannot handle relations. From “a horse is an animal” it follows that the head of a horse is the head of an animal, and, as Augustus De Morgan pointed out, no syllogism can prove it. Nor can it deal with statements that mix “every” and “some,” such as “everyone loves someone,” on which mathematics depends. In 1879 Gottlob Frege published a logic that could do all this, and Aristotle’s system became one small corner of it.
paras.zh: 有兩千年之久，亞里斯多德的邏輯被當成已經完成的學問。康德在 1787 年寫道，自亞里斯多德以來，邏輯沒有必要後退一步，也沒能前進一步。不到一百年後，它被證明只是一個片段。三段論處理由兩個詞項構成的陳述：「所有 A 都是 B」。它處理不了「關係」。從「馬是動物」可以推出「馬的頭是動物的頭」，而正如德摩根指出的，沒有任何三段論證得出這一點。它也對付不了混用「每一個」與「某一個」的陳述，例如「每個人都愛著某個人」，而數學正需要這種陳述。1879 年，弗雷格發表了一套能做到這一切的邏輯，亞里斯多德的系統成了其中的一個小角落。

paras.en: A second objection concerns his authority and not his logic. Because he was right about so much, his mistakes were protected for centuries: that heavier bodies fall faster, that the earth sits still at the center, that some people are slaves by nature and that women are naturally subordinate. The fault lies partly with his followers, since Aristotle himself held that argument must give way to observation. But the last two claims are his own, argued for in the Politics, and they show how a careful reasoner can mistake the arrangements of his own society for facts of nature.
paras.zh: 第二個反駁針對的是他的權威，不是他的邏輯。因為他對的地方太多，他的錯誤被保護了好幾個世紀：重的物體落得比較快；地球靜止在中心；有些人天生就是奴隸，而女人天生居於從屬。過錯有一部分在他的追隨者，因為亞里斯多德自己主張，論證必須向觀察讓步。但最後兩項是他本人的主張，在《政治學》裡有論證；它們顯示，一個細心的推理者可以怎樣把自己社會的安排，誤認為自然的事實。

problem.title_zh: 這些書是怎麼傳到我們手上的

paras.en: The treatises we read were probably never meant for publication. According to an ancient story, Aristotle’s manuscripts passed to Theophrastus and then to heirs who hid them in a cellar, where they lay for some two centuries before being brought to Rome and edited by Andronicus of Rhodes in the first century BCE. Whatever the truth of the story, the arrangement and many of the titles we use are the editor’s. “Metaphysics” itself is his label for the books placed after the Physics. In the Latin West most of Aristotle was then lost for centuries and returned in the twelfth and thirteenth centuries, largely through Arabic scholarship, with the commentaries of Ibn Sīnā and Ibn Rushd. To medieval readers he was simply “the Philosopher.”
paras.zh: 我們讀到的這些專論，大概從來不是為了出版而寫的。照一個古代的說法，亞里斯多德的手稿傳給泰奧弗拉斯托斯，再傳給後人，後人把它們藏在地窖裡，一放大約兩個世紀，才被帶到羅馬，在西元前一世紀由羅得島的安德羅尼科編訂。不管這個故事有幾分真，我們現在用的編排與許多書名都出自這位編者；「形上學」這個名字，就是他給排在《物理學》之後那幾卷書的標籤。此後在拉丁語的西方，亞里斯多德的大部分著作失傳了好幾個世紀，到十二、十三世紀才回來，而且主要是經由阿拉伯學術，連同伊本・西那與伊本・魯世德的註釋一起。對中世紀的讀者來說，他就叫「那位哲學家」。

said.claim: “We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act, but a habit.”
said.claim_zh: 「我們反覆做什麼，我們就是什麼。所以卓越不是一個行為，而是一種習慣。」
said.en: These are Will Durant’s words, from his summary of Aristotle’s ethics in The Story of Philosophy (1926). They paraphrase Nicomachean Ethics II.1–4, where Aristotle says that we become just by doing just acts and brave by doing brave acts. The summary is fair. The sentence is not Aristotle’s.
said.zh: 這是威爾・杜蘭的話，出自他在《哲學的故事》（1926）裡對亞里斯多德倫理學的摘要。它轉述的是《尼各馬可倫理學》卷二第一至四章；亞里斯多德在那裡說，我們因為做正義的事而成為正義的人，因為做勇敢的事而成為勇敢的人。這個摘要很公允，但句子不是亞里斯多德寫的。

paras.en: Two comparisons are often made, and both need care. The first is between Aristotle’s mean and the Buddha’s Middle Way. They share a shape and differ in substance. Aristotle’s mean is a point on a scale of feeling or action, different for each person and situation: the right amount of anger, the right amount of giving. The Middle Way (majjhimā paṭipadā) of the first sermon is a path between two ways of life, indulgence in sense pleasure and self-mortification, and it is spelled out as the eightfold path. Aristotle aims at the flourishing of a self. The Buddha’s path leads to seeing that there is no such self to flourish.
paras.zh: 常有人做兩個比較，兩個都需要小心。第一個是亞里斯多德的「中道」與佛陀的「中道」。兩者形狀相同，內容不同。亞里斯多德的中道是感受或行動量尺上的一個點，隨人、隨情境而不同：恰當分量的憤怒，恰當分量的施予。佛陀初轉法輪所說的中道（majjhimā paṭipadā），是兩種生活方式之間的一條路——耽於欲樂與自我折磨——並且具體展開為八正道。亞里斯多德瞄準的是一個自我的興盛；佛陀的道路通向的是看清：並沒有這樣一個可供興盛的自我。

paras.en: The second comparison is closer. Aristotle held that character is formed by repeated action: we become what we practice. Buddhist accounts of karma and of cultivation (bhāvanā) say much the same, and both traditions conclude that ethics is a matter of training and not only of knowing. That is the point on which both part company with Socrates. Which Western ethical theory Buddhist ethics most resembles, Aristotle’s or the utilitarians’, is a live debate among scholars (Dharma and the West, D18).
paras.zh: 第二個比較貼近得多。亞里斯多德主張，品格是由反覆的行動形成的：我們練習什麼，就成為什麼。佛教對業與修習（bhāvanā）的說明，講的幾乎是同一件事；兩個傳統都得出結論：倫理是訓練的事，不只是知道的事。在這一點上，兩者都跟蘇格拉底分道揚鑣。至於佛教倫理最像西方哪一種倫理學理論——亞里斯多德的，還是效益主義的——是學界正在進行的爭論（佛法與西方哲學 D18）。

terms.d_en: The traditional name for Aristotle’s six logical treatises.
terms.d_zh: 亞里斯多德六部邏輯專論的傳統總稱。

terms.d_en: Belonging to Aristotle’s school.
terms.d_zh: 屬於亞里斯多德學派的。

terms.d_en: Living and doing well over a whole life; often translated “happiness,” more exactly “flourishing.”
terms.d_zh: 在一整個人生中活得好、做得好；常譯「幸福」，更精確的說法是「興盛」。

terms.d_en: That for the sake of which a thing exists or is done; the root of “teleology.”
terms.d_zh: 事物存在或行為發生所為的目的；teleology（目的論）的字根。

terms.d_en: Material, formal, efficient, and final: four kinds of answer to the question why.
terms.d_zh: 質料因、形式因、動力因、目的因：對「為什麼」的四種回答。

terms.d_en: The right amount, between excess and deficiency, in feeling and action.
terms.d_zh: 感受與行動上，介於過與不及之間的恰當分量。

quiz.q: What was new about the Lyceum?
options: It worked as a research institute, with a library and collections.
It charged the highest fees in Athens.
It taught only mathematics.
It was open only to Athenian citizens.

quiz.q: What did Aristotle discover about arguments?
options: Whether a conclusion follows depends on the arrangement of terms, not on their meaning.
Only arguments about nature can be valid.
Every argument is circular.
Observation is unnecessary.

quiz.q: Why was Aristotle’s logic shown to be incomplete in the nineteenth century?
options: It could not handle relations or statements mixing “every” and “some.”
It contained a contradiction.
It had been mistranslated from Greek.
It relied on experiments.

further.t: Aristotle, Nicomachean Ethics, translated by W. D. Ross
further.n_en: Books I and II are the place to start.
further.n_zh: 從卷一、卷二讀起。

further.t: Aristotle, Prior Analytics, translated by A. J. Jenkinson
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, “Aristotle”

philosophers.name: René Descartes
philosophers.tag_en: He doubted everything he could, and from the one thing left tried to rebuild knowledge on the model of mathematics.
philosophers.tag_zh: 他懷疑了一切能懷疑的，再從僅存的那一樣東西出發，想照著數學的樣子重建知識。
facts: March 31, 1596, La Haye en Touraine, France
Jesuit college of La Flèche; law degree at Poitiers
The Dutch Republic for about twenty years
Discourse on Method (1637); Meditations (1641); Principles of Philosophy (1644)
Analytic geometry; the law of refraction

life.h_en: A good school and a restless graduate
life.h_zh: 一所好學校，一個坐不住的畢業生

paras.en: Descartes was born in 1596 in a small town in the Loire valley that has since been renamed after him. His mother died when he was a year old. At about ten he was sent to the Jesuit college of La Flèche, one of the best schools in Europe, where his delicate health earned him permission to stay in bed in the mornings, a habit he kept for life. He left with an excellent education and, by his own account, a sense that apart from mathematics he had learned nothing certain. He took a law degree to please his family and never practiced.
paras.zh: 笛卡兒 1596 年生於羅亞爾河谷的一個小鎮，那個鎮後來改以他的名字命名。他一歲時母親去世。大約十歲時，他被送進拉弗萊什的耶穌會學院，那是歐洲最好的學校之一；因為身體孱弱，他獲准早上賴在床上，這個習慣他保持了一輩子。他帶著極好的教育離開；而照他自己的說法，也帶著一種感覺：除了數學，他沒有學到任何確定的東西。為了讓家人高興，他拿了法律學位，卻從未執業。

paras.en: He resolved instead, as he put it, to study “the great book of the world,” and joined the army of a Dutch prince as a gentleman volunteer. On the night of November 10, 1619, shut up for the winter in a stove-heated room in Germany, he had three vivid dreams, which he took as a sign that his calling was to reform the whole of knowledge by a single method. It is a nice irony that the philosopher of the dream argument dated his vocation from a dream.
paras.zh: 他轉而決心，照他的說法，去讀「世界這本大書」，並以紳士志願兵的身分加入一位荷蘭親王的軍隊。1619 年 11 月 10 日夜裡，他在德國一間用火爐取暖的房間裡過冬，做了三個鮮明的夢；他把這些夢當作一個徵兆：他的天職是用單一的方法，改革全部的知識。提出夢之論證的哲學家，把自己的志業追溯到一場夢，這是個漂亮的反諷。

paras.en: In 1628 he moved to the Dutch Republic, the most tolerant country in Europe, and lived there for two decades, changing his address often and guarding his privacy. By 1633 he had finished a treatise on physics, The World, which assumed that the earth moves. Then came the news that Galileo had been condemned in Rome for teaching the same thing, and Descartes suppressed the book. Caution shaped everything he published afterward.
paras.zh: 1628 年他搬到荷蘭共和國，當時歐洲最寬容的國家，在那裡住了二十年，經常換住址，小心守著自己的隱私。到 1633 年，他已經完成一部物理學專論《論世界》，書中假定地球在動。接著傳來消息：伽利略因為教同樣的東西，在羅馬被定了罪。笛卡兒把這本書壓了下來。此後他發表的一切，都帶著謹慎的痕跡。

paras.en: In 1637 he brought out the Discourse on Method, written in French so that, as he said, even women might read it. It came with three scientific essays, one of which, the Geometry, showed how curves can be described by equations and so joined algebra to geometry. The Meditations followed in 1641. He took the unusual step of circulating the manuscript beforehand to critics, among them Thomas Hobbes and the theologian Antoine Arnauld, and printing their objections together with his replies.
paras.zh: 1637 年他出版了《談談方法》，用法文寫成；照他的說法，這樣連婦女也讀得懂。書後附了三篇科學論文，其中一篇〈幾何學〉說明了曲線可以怎樣用方程式來描述，就此把代數與幾何接了起來。《沉思集》在 1641 年問世。他採取了一個不尋常的做法：事先把手稿送給批評者傳閱，其中有霍布斯與神學家阿爾諾，然後把他們的反駁連同自己的答覆一起印出來。

life.h_en: A princess, a queen, and a cold climate
life.h_zh: 一位公主、一位女王、一個寒冷的國度

paras.en: His most searching critic was a young exile, Princess Elisabeth of Bohemia, who wrote to him in 1643 to ask how an immaterial mind could possibly move a material body. Their correspondence lasted until his death, and his last book, The Passions of the Soul, grew out of it. In 1649 Queen Christina of Sweden persuaded him to come to Stockholm as her tutor. She wanted her lessons at five in the morning, in an unheated library, during one of the coldest winters on record. The man who had spent every morning of his life in bed caught pneumonia and died on February 11, 1650, aged fifty-three.
paras.zh: 對他提出最深入質疑的，是一位年輕的流亡者：波希米亞的伊莉莎白公主。她在 1643 年寫信問他：一個非物質的心靈，到底怎麼可能推動一個物質的身體？兩人的通信持續到他去世，他的最後一本書《論靈魂的激情》就是從這些通信長出來的。1649 年，瑞典女王克里斯蒂娜說服他到斯德哥爾摩當她的老師。她要在清晨五點上課，在一間沒有暖氣的圖書室裡，而那是有紀錄以來最冷的冬天之一。這個一輩子每天早上都待在床上的人染上了肺炎，在 1650 年 2 月 11 日去世，享年五十三歲。

idea.title_en: The central idea: Mind and body are two kinds of thing
idea.title_zh: 核心觀念：心與身是兩種東西

paras.en: Descartes is remembered for a method and for a doctrine, and the second follows from the first. The method is to accept only what is perceived so clearly and distinctly that it cannot be doubted, and to build on it step by step, as a geometer builds on axioms. The cogito is the first such truth. From it he draws the doctrine known as dualism. He can doubt that he has a body and cannot doubt that he is thinking. He concludes that he is essentially a thinking thing (res cogitans), whose whole nature is to think, and that body is a different kind of thing altogether (res extensa), whose whole nature is to take up space.
paras.zh: 笛卡兒被後人記得的，是一套方法與一個學說，而後者是從前者來的。方法是：只接受被知覺得如此「清楚而分明」、以致無法懷疑的東西，然後一步一步往上蓋，就像幾何學家從公理往上蓋。Cogito 是第一個這樣的真理。他從它引出了稱為「二元論」的學說。他可以懷疑自己有身體，卻無法懷疑自己在思考。他的結論是：他本質上是一個思考的東西（res cogitans），其全部本性就是思考；而物體是完全不同的另一種東西（res extensa），其全部本性就是佔有空間。

paras.en: The division did an enormous amount of work. It handed the whole material world, including animal and human bodies, to mechanical physics, and so helped to make modern science possible. And it kept the mind, with its freedom and its claim to immortality, out of the reach of that physics. Almost every later debate about consciousness starts from the picture he drew, usually in order to escape it.
paras.zh: 這個劃分做了極大量的工作。它把整個物質世界，包括動物與人的身體在內，交給了機械論的物理學，因而促成了現代科學。同時，它把心靈連同心靈的自由、以及它對不朽的主張，放在那門物理學碰不到的地方。後來幾乎每一場關於意識的爭論，都是從他畫出的這幅圖像出發的；而出發的目的，通常是為了逃離它。

quote.en: I am, I exist, is necessarily true each time it is expressed by me, or conceived in my mind.
quote.zh: 「我是，我存在」，每當我說出它、或在心裡想到它的時候，必然是真的。
quote.ref: Descartes, Meditations II, tr. John Veitch
quote.note_en: The one certainty left at the bottom of the doubt.
quote.note_zh: 懷疑到最底層，僅存的那一個確定。

objection.title_en: The strongest objection: How do the two interact?
objection.title_zh: 最強的反駁：這兩者怎麼互相作用？

paras.en: Princess Elisabeth saw the difficulty at once. On Descartes’ own physics, a body is moved only by being pushed, and pushing requires contact between things that have surfaces. A mind has no size, shape, or location. How, then, does my decision to raise my arm raise it, and how does a pin in my finger produce a feeling of pain? Descartes suggested that the exchange takes place in the pineal gland, a small organ at the center of the brain. That says where the interaction happens and leaves the question of how it happens untouched. He never gave Elisabeth an answer she accepted, and in the end he told her, more or less, not to think about it too much.
paras.zh: 伊莉莎白公主一眼就看出了困難。照笛卡兒自己的物理學，物體只有被推才會動，而推需要有表面的東西彼此接觸。心靈沒有大小、形狀或位置。那麼，我「舉起手臂」的決定是怎麼把手臂舉起來的？扎在我手指上的針，又是怎麼產生「痛」的感覺的？笛卡兒提出，這種交流發生在松果腺，腦部中央的一個小器官。這說的是互動「在哪裡」發生，對「怎麼」發生的問題完全沒有碰到。他始終沒有給伊莉莎白一個她接受的答案；到最後，他差不多是告訴她：別想太多。

paras.en: A second objection goes to the method. Descartes needs God to guarantee that what he perceives clearly and distinctly is true. But his proof that God exists relies on premises he accepts because he perceives them clearly and distinctly. Arnauld pointed out the circle in 1641, and it has been called the Cartesian circle ever since.
paras.zh: 第二個反駁針對的是方法。笛卡兒需要上帝來保證，他清楚而分明地知覺到的東西是真的。可是他對「上帝存在」的證明所依賴的前提，他之所以接受，正是因為他清楚而分明地知覺到了它們。阿爾諾在 1641 年指出了這個循環；從此它就被稱為「笛卡兒循環」。

paras.en: Unlike Socrates and Aristotle, Descartes controlled how he was read. He chose his own genres with care: an intellectual autobiography in the Discourse, a set of spiritual exercises in the Meditations, a textbook in the Principles. He also published his critics alongside himself, so that the Objections and Replies is several times the length of the work it discusses. After his death the Catholic Church placed his books on the Index of prohibited works in 1663. Within a century “Cartesian” had become the name of the old orthodoxy that Newton and Locke set out to overturn.
paras.zh: 跟蘇格拉底與亞里斯多德不同，笛卡兒掌控了自己被閱讀的方式。他仔細挑選自己的文體：《談談方法》是一部知性自傳，《沉思集》是一套靈修式的練習，《哲學原理》是一本教科書。他還把批評者跟自己並排出版，以致《反駁與答辯》的篇幅是它所討論的正文的好幾倍。他去世之後，天主教會在 1663 年把他的著作列入禁書目錄。不到一個世紀，「笛卡兒派」就成了舊正統的名字，是牛頓與洛克著手要推翻的對象。

said.claim: Descartes invented coordinates while watching a fly walk across his ceiling.
said.claim_zh: 笛卡兒看著一隻蒼蠅在天花板上爬，發明了座標。
said.en: The story is told in many schoolbooks, and no source from his lifetime supports it. The Geometry of 1637 does show how to describe a curve by an equation, which is the decisive idea. It does not use a pair of perpendicular axes in the modern way, and negative coordinates came later. The “Cartesian plane” is named in his honor and is not found in his book.
said.zh: 許多教科書都講這個故事，但沒有任何他在世時的資料可以佐證。1637 年的〈幾何學〉確實說明了怎樣用方程式描述曲線，這是決定性的想法。它並沒有照現代的方式使用一對互相垂直的軸，負座標也是後來才有的。「笛卡兒平面」是為了紀念他而命名的，在他的書裡找不到。

paras.en: Both men begin by turning attention inward and asking what can be found there, and they report opposite findings. Descartes looks within and finds a self: a single, lasting, thinking substance that is more certain than anything else. The Buddha looks within and finds form, feeling, perception, volitional formations, and consciousness, the five aggregates, each arising and passing, and no owner among them. Hume, a century after Descartes, repeated the experiment and sided with the Buddha: when he entered most intimately into what he called himself, he always stumbled on some particular perception and never caught a self without one.
paras.zh: 這兩個人都從把注意力轉向內在開始，問在那裡找得到什麼；而他們報告的結果相反。笛卡兒往內看，找到一個自我：一個單一、持存、會思考的實體，比其他任何東西都確定。佛陀往內看，找到的是色、受、想、行、識，也就是五蘊，各自生起、各自滅去，其中沒有主人。在笛卡兒之後一個世紀，休謨重做了這個實驗，站到了佛陀這一邊：當他最貼近地進入他稱為「自己」的東西時，他總是碰到某個個別的知覺，從來沒有在沒有知覺的情況下抓到一個自我。

paras.en: On mind and body the comparison is less direct. Early Buddhism distinguishes nāma, the mental, from rūpa, the material, which sounds like dualism. But neither is a substance. Both are processes, and in one well-known simile name-and-form and consciousness are said to depend on each other in the way that two sheaves of reeds stand by leaning together (Saṃyutta Nikāya 12.67). Elisabeth’s question, how two utterly different substances can act on each other, does not arise in that form, because there are no substances to begin with.
paras.zh: 在心與身的問題上，比較就沒有那麼直接。早期佛教區分 nāma（名，心理的）與 rūpa（色，物質的），聽起來像二元論。但兩者都不是實體。兩者都是過程；在一個著名的比喻裡，名色與識被說成互相依待，就像兩束蘆葦靠在一起才立得住（《相應部》12.67）。伊莉莎白的問題——兩種截然不同的實體怎麼能互相作用——不會以那種形式出現，因為打從一開始就沒有實體。

terms.d_en: The view that mind and body are two distinct kinds of thing.
terms.d_zh: 主張心與身是兩種不同的東西。

terms.d_en: A thing that exists in its own right and bears properties.
terms.d_zh: 憑自身而存在、並且承載性質的東西。

terms.d_en: Descartes’ names for mind and for body.
terms.d_zh: 笛卡兒對心靈與物體的稱呼。

terms.d_en: His mark of truth: a perception so evident that one cannot doubt it while attending to it.
terms.d_zh: 他的真理標記：一個知覺明白到只要專注於它，就無法懷疑它。

terms.o: L. Cartesius, the Latin form of his name
terms.d_en: The charge that he uses clear and distinct perception to prove God, and God to validate clear and distinct perception.
terms.d_zh: 這項指控：他用清楚分明的知覺證明上帝，又用上帝保證清楚分明的知覺。

terms.d_en: The difficulty of explaining how an immaterial mind and a material body affect each other.
terms.d_zh: 如何解釋非物質的心靈與物質的身體互相影響，這個難題。

quiz.q: Why did Descartes suppress his treatise The World in 1633?
options: Galileo had just been condemned for teaching that the earth moves.
He had found a mathematical error in it.
Queen Christina asked him to.
The manuscript was lost in a fire.

quiz.q: What does Cartesian dualism claim?
options: Mind and body are two distinct kinds of thing.
There are two gods.
Every argument has two sides.
The mind is a part of the brain.

quiz.q: What was Princess Elisabeth’s objection?
options: An immaterial mind has no way of pushing a material body.
The cogito is circular.
Dreams cannot be vivid.
God cannot be proved.

further.t: René Descartes, Discourse on Method, translated by John Veitch
further.n_en: Short, autobiographical, and written to be enjoyed. Parts 1 to 4.
further.n_zh: 短、帶自傳性、寫來就是要讓人讀得愉快的。讀第一到四部分。

further.t: René Descartes, Meditations on First Philosophy, translated by John Veitch
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, “René Descartes” and “Elisabeth, Princess of Bohemia”

philosophers.name: Plato
philosophers.tag_en: Socrates’ pupil and Aristotle’s teacher, who turned philosophy into literature and founded the first university.
philosophers.tag_zh: 蘇格拉底的學生、亞里斯多德的老師；他把哲學寫成了文學，並且創辦了第一所大學。
facts: c. 428 BCE, Athens, to an aristocratic family
About thirty-five dialogues, all of which survive

life.h_en: A young man with a political future
life.h_zh: 一個前途在政壇的年輕人

paras.en: Plato was born in Athens around 428 BCE, a few years into the long war with Sparta, into one of the city’s oldest families. On his mother’s side he was related to Solon, the lawgiver. Everything pointed to a career in politics. Two things turned him from it. The first was the conduct of his own relatives: when Athens lost the war in 404, an oligarchy of thirty seized power, two of his kinsmen were among its leaders, and it ruled by murder. The second was what the restored democracy did five years later, when it tried and executed Socrates, whom Plato, then about twenty-eight, considered the most just man of his time.
paras.zh: 柏拉圖大約西元前 428 年生於雅典，當時對斯巴達的長年戰爭才開打幾年；他出身城裡最古老的家族之一，母親那邊跟立法者梭倫有親戚關係。一切都指向政治生涯。有兩件事讓他轉了向。第一件是他自己親戚的作為：西元前 404 年雅典戰敗，三十人的寡頭集團奪權，他有兩位親屬名列領袖，而這個政權靠殺戮統治。第二件是五年後恢復的民主政體做的事：它審判並處死了蘇格拉底；當時大約二十八歲的柏拉圖，認為蘇格拉底是那個時代最正義的人。

paras.en: A letter that has come down under his name, and may be genuine, describes the result. He concluded that every existing city was badly governed, and that the troubles of mankind would not end until philosophers became rulers or rulers became philosophers. He left Athens for some years and traveled, probably to southern Italy, where he met followers of Pythagoras and absorbed their conviction that mathematics is the key to reality.
paras.zh: 一封以他的名義流傳下來、有可能是真作的信，描述了這件事的結果。他斷定，現存的每一個城邦都治理得很糟；人類的禍患，要等到哲學家成為統治者、或統治者成為哲學家，才會終止。他離開雅典幾年，四處遊歷，大概到過義大利南部，在那裡遇見畢達哥拉斯的追隨者，並且吸收了他們的信念：數學是通往實在的鑰匙。

paras.en: Around 387 he returned and founded a school in a grove outside the walls that was sacred to the hero Academus. The Academy had no fees and no fixed curriculum, and it lasted, in one form or another, for the better part of nine centuries. A later tradition says that over its door were the words “Let no one ignorant of geometry enter.” The story cannot be traced back to Plato’s own time, but it suits a school where leading mathematicians worked beside philosophers. Its most famous member arrived at seventeen and stayed twenty years: Aristotle.
paras.zh: 大約西元前 387 年他回到雅典，在城牆外一座獻給英雄阿卡德摩斯的樹林裡辦了一所學校。學院不收學費，也沒有固定的課程；它以各種形式存續了將近九個世紀。後來有個傳說，說它門上寫著：「不懂幾何學的人不得入內。」這個說法追溯不到柏拉圖自己的時代，但它跟這所學校很相稱：頂尖的數學家在那裡跟哲學家並肩工作。學院最有名的成員十七歲入學，待了二十年：亞里斯多德。

paras.en: Plato tested his political ideas once in practice, and it went badly. He was invited to Syracuse, the richest city in the Greek West, to educate its young ruler Dionysius II as a philosopher-king. The pupil lost interest, the court turned hostile, and Plato was for a time kept there against his will. He went back to teaching and writing, and his last and longest work, the Laws, is a far more cautious book than the Republic.
paras.zh: 柏拉圖把他的政治理念付諸實踐過一次，結果很糟。他受邀前往敘拉古——希臘世界西部最富有的城邦——要把年輕的統治者狄奧尼修斯二世教育成哲學家國王。學生失去了興趣，宮廷轉為敵意，柏拉圖有一段時間被違背意願地留在那裡。他回去繼續教書寫作；他最後、也是最長的一部作品《法律篇》，比《理想國》謹慎得多。

paras.en: He wrote dialogues, and never appears in them as a speaker. In the early ones Socrates questions people and nothing is settled. In the middle ones, the Phaedo, the Symposium, and the Republic, Socrates sets out bold doctrines about the soul and the Forms. In the late ones those doctrines are examined critically, sometimes by a character who defeats Socrates in argument. A reader therefore never knows for certain what Plato believed, and it is likely that he intended this. He had learned from his teacher that a conclusion one has been handed is worth much less than a conclusion one has been made to reach. All of his dialogues survive, which is true of almost no other ancient author.
paras.zh: 他寫的是對話錄，而且從不讓自己在其中開口。在早期的對話錄裡，蘇格拉底詰問別人，最後什麼都沒有定論。在中期的《斐多篇》《會飲篇》《理想國》裡，蘇格拉底提出關於靈魂與理型的大膽學說。在晚期的對話錄裡，這些學說受到批判性的檢視，有時檢視者是一個在論證上擊敗蘇格拉底的角色。所以讀者永遠無法確定柏拉圖本人相信什麼，而這很可能是他有意如此。他從老師那裡學到：別人交到你手上的結論，價值遠遠不如你被引導著自己得出的結論。他的對話錄全部流傳了下來；幾乎沒有別的古代作者有這樣的運氣。

timeline: Aristotle arrives; first voyage to Dionysius II
亞里斯多德入學；首次赴狄奧尼修斯二世處

paras.en: Socrates had asked what courage is, or justice, and had found that nobody could say. Plato took the question to have an answer, and asked what sort of thing the answer could be. It cannot be any particular brave act, since each of those is brave in some ways and circumstances and not in others. It must be something that all brave acts share and none of them fully is. He called such a thing a Form (eidos). The Form of Beauty is beautiful without qualification, does not come into being or pass away, and is the same for everyone. Particular beautiful things are beautiful by “sharing in” it, as many reflections share in one face.
paras.zh: 蘇格拉底問過勇敢是什麼、正義是什麼，結果發現沒有人說得出來。柏拉圖認定這個問題是有答案的，於是進一步問：這個答案可能是哪一種東西？它不可能是任何一個個別的勇敢行為，因為那些行為各自只在某些方面、某些情境下是勇敢的，在別的方面則不是。它必定是所有勇敢行為共有、卻沒有哪一個完全就是的東西。他把這樣的東西叫作「理型」（eidos）。「美的理型」是無條件地美，不生不滅，對每個人都一樣。個別的美的事物之所以美，是因為「分有」了它，就像許多倒影分有同一張臉。

paras.en: The theory was meant to do several jobs at once. It explains how we can have knowledge although the world we perceive is in flux. It explains how one word, “just,” can apply correctly to many different things. It gives ethics an objective standard, independent of what any person or city happens to approve. And, joined to the view that the soul knew the Forms before birth, it explains how we can recognize a truth we were never taught. The philosopher Alfred North Whitehead remarked that the European philosophical tradition “consists of a series of footnotes to Plato,” and what he had in mind was this range of questions more than any of the answers.
paras.zh: 這個理論原本要同時完成好幾項工作。它解釋了，儘管我們感知的世界流變不居，我們為什麼還能有知識。它解釋了，「正義」這一個詞，為什麼能正確地用在許多不同的事物上。它給了倫理學一個客觀的標準，不取決於任何個人或城邦碰巧贊同什麼。再配上「靈魂在出生之前就認識理型」這個看法，它還解釋了，我們為什麼能認出一個從來沒有人教過我們的真理。哲學家懷海德說過，歐洲的哲學傳統「是由對柏拉圖的一連串註腳構成的」；他心裡想的，與其說是柏拉圖的哪一個答案，不如說是這一整片問題。

quote.en: To them, I said, the truth would be literally nothing but the shadows of the images.
quote.zh: 我說，對他們來說，真實簡直就只是那些造像的影子。
quote.note_en: Socrates, describing the prisoners in the cave.
quote.note_zh: 蘇格拉底描述洞穴裡的囚徒。

objection.title_en: The strongest objection: The Third Man

paras.en: The most damaging criticism of the Forms was written by Plato. In the Parmenides a young Socrates presents the theory to the old philosopher Parmenides, who takes it apart. Suppose many things are large, and we explain this by a single Form, Largeness, in which they share. Is Largeness itself large? It seems it must be, since it is what largeness is. But then the large things and the Form of Largeness are all large, and by the same reasoning there must be a second Form to explain what they have in common, and then a third, without end. The theory was supposed to explain the many by the one, and it has produced infinitely many ones.
paras.zh: 對理型論殺傷力最大的批評，是柏拉圖自己寫的。在《巴門尼德篇》裡，年輕的蘇格拉底向年老的哲學家巴門尼德提出這個理論，而巴門尼德把它拆了。假設有許多東西是大的，我們用一個單一的理型「大」來解釋，說它們分有了它。那麼「大」本身大不大？看來它必定是大的，因為它就是「大」之所以為大。可是這樣一來，那些大的東西加上「大的理型」全都是大的；照同樣的推理，必須有第二個理型來解釋它們的共同之處，然後是第三個，沒有盡頭。這個理論本來要用「一」來解釋「多」，結果它產生了無窮多個「一」。

paras.en: Aristotle added a second objection that is simpler and may be worse. Even if the Forms exist, they explain nothing. A separate, unchanging Form of Horse does not make horses, move them, or help us learn about them, and “sharing in” is, he said, an empty phrase and a poetic metaphor. What makes a horse a horse must be in the horse. Plato went on defending and revising the theory to the end of his life, and never answered these objections to everyone’s satisfaction, his own included.
paras.zh: 亞里斯多德加了第二個反駁，比較簡單，也許更致命。就算理型存在，它們也什麼都沒解釋。一個分離而不變的「馬的理型」既不造馬、不推動馬，也無助於我們認識馬；至於「分有」，他說那是空話，是詩的比喻。使馬成為馬的東西，一定在馬裡面。柏拉圖直到生命結束都在捍衛並修訂這個理論，而始終沒有把這些反駁回答到讓每個人滿意的地步，包括他自己。

problem.title_en: Reading an author who never speaks
problem.title_zh: 讀一位從不開口的作者

paras.en: With Plato the difficulty is the opposite of the one we met with Socrates. We have everything he published, and we still cannot be sure of his views, because he says nothing in his own voice. Scholars divide the dialogues into early, middle, and late, partly by their content and partly by statistical studies of his prose style, and most agree that the Socrates of the early group is closest to the historical man, while the Socrates of the Republic speaks for Plato. Ancient reports add a further puzzle. Aristotle refers to Plato’s “unwritten doctrines,” and in one dialogue Plato has Socrates argue that serious thought cannot be entrusted to writing at all, since a book cannot answer questions and says the same thing to every reader.
paras.zh: 讀柏拉圖的困難，跟我們在蘇格拉底那裡遇到的正好相反。他發表過的東西我們全都有，卻仍然無法確定他的看法，因為他從不用自己的聲音說話。學者把對話錄分成早、中、晚三期，一部分依據內容，一部分依據對他散文風格的統計研究；多數人同意，早期那一組裡的蘇格拉底最接近歷史上的那個人，而《理想國》裡的蘇格拉底是在替柏拉圖發言。古代的記載又添了一個謎。亞里斯多德提到柏拉圖的「未成文學說」；而柏拉圖在一部對話錄裡，讓蘇格拉底論證說：嚴肅的思想根本不能託付給文字，因為書不會回答問題，而且對每個讀者說的都是同一套。

said.claim: Plato’s real name was Aristocles; “Plato” was a nickname meaning “broad.”
said.claim_zh: 柏拉圖的本名是亞里斯托克勒斯；「柏拉圖」是綽號，意思是「寬」。
said.en: The story comes from Diogenes Laertius, who wrote more than five hundred years after Plato’s death and offers three different explanations of the nickname: broad shoulders, a broad forehead, a broad style. Plato was in fact an ordinary Athenian name of the period, and many scholars now think the tale was invented later.
said.zh: 這個說法出自第歐根尼・拉爾修，他寫作的時間在柏拉圖去世五百多年之後，而且對這個綽號給了三種不同的解釋：肩膀寬、額頭寬、文風寬廣。事實上「柏拉圖」在當時是個普通的雅典名字；現在許多學者認為，這個故事是後來編出來的。

paras.en: The two agree about the starting point and disagree about nearly everything after it. Both hold that ordinary experience is a kind of captivity, that its cause is a failure to see, and that release comes through a disciplined turning of the whole person, which involves conduct as well as intellect. Both also teach that the one who is free should go back for the others.
paras.zh: 這兩個人對起點的看法一致，對起點之後幾乎每一件事的看法都不同。兩人都主張：平常的經驗是一種被囚的狀態，原因是沒有看見，而解脫要靠整個人有紀律的轉向，這個轉向既涉及行為也涉及理智。兩人也都教導：得到自由的人，應該為了其他人回去。

paras.en: The disagreement concerns what there is to be seen. Plato’s answer to change is permanence. Behind the flux stand eternal Forms, and the soul that knows them is itself immortal and akin to them. The Buddha’s teaching goes the other way on each of these points. All conditioned things are impermanent, no unchanging essence is to be found in them, and the search for a permanent self is the root of the trouble. A Platonist tries to escape from the changing to the changeless. A Buddhist tries to see change clearly enough to stop grasping at it. It is hard to find two great traditions that describe the human problem so alike and then prescribe such opposite cures.
paras.zh: 分歧在於：有什麼可以被看見？柏拉圖對變化的回答是恆常。在流變的背後有永恆的理型；認識理型的靈魂，本身也是不朽的，並且與理型同類。佛陀的教導在這幾點上，每一點都走相反的方向。一切有為法都是無常的，其中找不到不變的本質，而追尋一個恆常的自我，正是問題的根源。柏拉圖主義者想從變動逃向不變。佛教徒想把變化看得夠清楚，清楚到不再去抓取它。很難找到另外兩個偉大的傳統，把人的問題描述得如此相似，開出的藥方卻如此相反。

terms.d_en: An eternal, unchanging reality of which particular things are copies.
terms.d_zh: 永恆不變的實在，個別事物是它的仿製品。

terms.d_en: The relation of a particular thing to its Form.
terms.d_zh: 個別事物與其理型之間的關係。

terms.d_en: Philosophical inquiry by question and answer; in the Republic, the highest study.
terms.d_zh: 以問答進行的哲學探究；在《理想國》裡是最高的學問。

terms.d_en: The doctrine that learning is recovering knowledge the soul had before birth.
terms.d_zh: 主張學習是找回靈魂在出生前已有的知識。

terms.d_en: The ruler of Plato’s ideal city, who governs because he knows the Good.
terms.d_zh: 柏拉圖理想城邦的統治者，因為認識「善」而治理。

terms.d_en: Any view holding that abstract objects, such as numbers, exist independently of minds and of the physical world.
terms.d_zh: 凡是主張抽象對象（例如數）獨立於心靈與物質世界而存在的看法。

quiz.q: Which two events turned Plato away from a career in politics?
options: The rule of the Thirty and the execution of Socrates.
The plague and the death of Pericles.
The founding of the Academy and his voyages to Sicily.
The Persian invasion and the battle of Marathon.

quiz.q: What is a Form, in Plato’s theory?
options: An unchanging reality that particular things imperfectly resemble.
The physical shape of an object.
A rule of grammar.
A kind of government.

quiz.q: What does the Third Man argument claim?
options: Explaining likeness by a Form leads to an endless series of further Forms.
A third person is needed to judge any debate.
There were three men named Socrates.
The Forms are located in the brain.

further.t: Plato, Republic, translated by Benjamin Jowett
further.n_en: Books I, VI, and VII if you read nothing else.
further.n_zh: 如果只讀一部分，讀第一、六、七卷。

further.t: Plato, Symposium, translated by Benjamin Jowett
further.n_en: On love; the most beautiful of the dialogues.
further.n_zh: 談愛；對話錄裡最美的一部。

further.t: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, “Plato”

philosophers.name: John Locke
philosophers.tag_en: A physician who asked what the human mind is fit to know, and whose answers shaped modern science, schooling, and government.
philosophers.tag_zh: 一位醫生，問了「人的心靈適合知道什麼」；他的回答塑造了現代的科學、教育與政府。
facts: An Essay Concerning Human Understanding; Two Treatises of Government; A Letter Concerning Toleration

paras.en: Locke was born in 1632 in a Somerset village, the son of a country lawyer who fought on Parliament’s side in the English Civil War. He was ten when the war began and sixteen, a schoolboy at Westminster, when King Charles I was beheaded a short walk from his classroom. At Oxford he found the official curriculum, still the philosophy of Aristotle’s medieval followers, tedious and useless. What caught his interest was the new experimental science. He worked with the chemist Robert Boyle, read Descartes, and trained as a physician.
paras.zh: 洛克 1632 年生於薩默塞特郡的一個村莊，父親是鄉村律師，在英國內戰中站在議會這一邊作戰。戰爭開始時他十歲；十六歲時他是西敏公學的學生，國王查理一世就在離他教室不遠的地方被斬首。在牛津，他覺得官方課程——仍然是亞里斯多德的中世紀追隨者那一套哲學——沉悶而無用。吸引他的是新興的實驗科學。他跟化學家波以耳一起工作，讀笛卡兒，並且受訓成為醫生。

life.h_en: A patron, a plot, and exile
life.h_zh: 一位恩主、一場陰謀、一段流亡

paras.en: In 1666 a chance meeting changed his life. Lord Ashley, later Earl of Shaftesbury and one of the most powerful politicians in England, came to Oxford for his health, liked Locke, and took him into his household as physician and secretary. Two years later Locke supervised a dangerous operation to drain an abscess on Ashley’s liver, and the patient credited him with saving his life. Through Shaftesbury, Locke was drawn into the great political struggle of the age, the effort to limit the power of the crown and to keep a Catholic heir from the throne.
paras.zh: 1666 年，一次偶然的會面改變了他的人生。艾希利勳爵——後來的沙夫茨伯里伯爵、英格蘭最有權勢的政治人物之一——為了養病來到牛津，很欣賞洛克，把他請進府裡擔任醫生兼秘書。兩年後，洛克主持了一場危險的手術，為艾希利肝臟上的膿瘍引流；病人認為是他救了自己一命。經由沙夫茨伯里，洛克被捲進那個時代最大的政治鬥爭：限制王權，並且阻止一位天主教繼承人登上王位。

paras.en: When that effort failed and turned to conspiracy, Shaftesbury fled abroad and died. Locke, under suspicion, followed him to the Dutch Republic in 1683 and lived there for more than five years, some of the time under a false name. He used the time to finish the book he had been drafting for nearly two decades. It had begun, he says, at a meeting of five or six friends whose discussion kept running into difficulties, until it occurred to him that before going further they ought to examine what the human understanding was and was not fitted to deal with.
paras.zh: 這番努力失敗、轉為密謀之後，沙夫茨伯里逃往國外，隨即去世。洛克受到懷疑，1683 年跟著逃到荷蘭共和國，在那裡住了五年多，有段時間用的是假名。他利用這段時間，完成了那本已經起草將近二十年的書。照他的說法，那本書始於五六個朋友的一次聚會；他們的討論老是陷入困難，直到他想到：在繼續往下談之前，應該先檢查一下，人的理解力適合處理什麼、不適合處理什麼。

paras.en: The revolution of 1688 put a Protestant king on the throne under conditions set by Parliament, and Locke came home in the same fleet as the new queen. Within a year he published the three works on which his fame rests: An Essay Concerning Human Understanding, which appeared under his name; and the Two Treatises of Government and A Letter Concerning Toleration, which he published anonymously and acknowledged only in his will. He was fifty-seven and had printed almost nothing before.
paras.zh: 1688 年的革命，讓一位新教國王在議會設定的條件下登上王位；洛克跟新王后搭同一支船隊回國。一年之內，他出版了奠定他名聲的三部作品：《人類理解論》，具名發表；《政府論兩篇》與《論寬容書簡》，匿名出版，他只在遺囑裡承認是自己寫的。當時他五十七歲，此前幾乎沒有印行過任何東西。

paras.en: He spent his last years at Oates, the Essex home of Damaris Masham, a philosopher herself, where he wrote on education, money, and the Bible, served on the government’s Board of Trade, and answered his critics. He died there in 1704 while Lady Masham read the Psalms to him.
paras.zh: 他晚年住在艾塞克斯郡的奧茨，那是達瑪麗斯・馬沙姆夫人的家，她自己也是一位哲學家。他在那裡寫作，談教育、貨幣與《聖經》，任職於政府的貿易委員會，並且回應批評他的人。1704 年他在那裡去世，當時馬沙姆夫人正為他朗讀〈詩篇〉。

timeline: Returns to England; publishes the three great works
返回英格蘭；出版三部主要著作

idea.title_en: The central idea: Experience is the only source of ideas
idea.title_zh: 核心觀念：經驗是觀念唯一的來源

paras.en: Locke’s project is to trace the contents of the mind back to their origins and so to mark out the limits of what we can know. Everything the mind works with he calls an idea. Simple ideas, such as yellow, cold, or the idea of thinking, come in through sensation and reflection and cannot be invented. Complex ideas, such as gold, justice, or infinity, are made by the mind from simple ones. Where our ideas run out, so does our knowledge, and Locke is willing to say that this happens often. We do not know the real inner constitution of material things, or how matter could think, and in most of life we must be content with probability. He described himself as an under-laborer, clearing away some of the rubbish that lies in the way of knowledge, while Boyle and Newton did the building.
paras.zh: 洛克的計畫是把心靈的內容追溯到它們的源頭，從而標出我們所能知道的界限。心靈所處理的一切，他稱為「觀念」。簡單觀念，例如黃、冷，或「思考」這個觀念，是經由感覺與反省進來的，沒辦法憑空發明。複雜觀念，例如黃金、正義、無限，是心靈用簡單觀念造出來的。我們的觀念在哪裡用完，我們的知識就在哪裡用完；而洛克願意承認，這種情況經常發生。我們不知道物質事物真正的內在構造，也不知道物質怎麼可能思考；在人生的大部分事情上，我們只能滿足於或然性。他形容自己是個打下手的小工，清掉一些擋在知識路上的垃圾，而蓋房子的是波以耳與牛頓。

paras.en: The same temper marks his politics. Because nobody is born with a title to rule or with knowledge of the one true religion, government has to rest on the consent of the governed, and belief cannot rightly be forced. People are by nature free and equal, and reason teaches that “no one ought to harm another in his life, health, liberty, or possessions.” A government that breaks this trust may be resisted. The men who wrote the American Declaration of Independence had read him closely.
paras.zh: 同樣的性格也表現在他的政治思想上。因為沒有人生來就有統治的名分，也沒有人生來就知道哪一個才是唯一的真宗教，所以政府必須建立在被治者的同意之上，而信仰不能正當地被強迫。人天生是自由而平等的；理性教導我們：「任何人都不應該侵害他人的生命、健康、自由或財物。」背棄這份託付的政府，人民可以抵抗。起草美國《獨立宣言》的那些人，仔細讀過他。

quote.en: No man’s knowledge here can go beyond his experience.
quote.zh: 在這裡，沒有人的知識能夠超出他的經驗。
quote.ref: Locke, An Essay Concerning Human Understanding II.i.19
quote.note_en: Said of our knowledge of our own minds, and often taken as the motto of empiricism.
quote.note_zh: 原是就我們對自己心靈的認識而說的，常被當作經驗主義的座右銘。

objection.title_en: The strongest objection: The veil of ideas
objection.title_zh: 最強的反駁：觀念的帷幕

paras.en: On Locke’s account the mind never perceives things directly. What it perceives are its own ideas, which things cause in it. He distinguished primary qualities, such as shape, size, and motion, which he thought really belong to objects, from secondary qualities, such as color, taste, and warmth, which are only powers in objects to produce certain ideas in us. The ideas of primary qualities resemble their causes, he said, and the ideas of secondary qualities do not.
paras.zh: 照洛克的說法，心靈從來不是直接知覺到事物的。它知覺到的是自己的觀念，而觀念是事物在它裡面引起的。他區分了初性——例如形狀、大小、運動，他認為這些確實屬於物體——與次性——例如顏色、味道、溫熱，這些只是物體在我們身上引起某些觀念的「能力」。他說，初性的觀念與它們的原因相似，次性的觀念則不然。

paras.en: George Berkeley, a generation later, asked the fatal question. If all we ever perceive is ideas, how could we check whether any of them resembles a thing outside the mind? Comparing an idea with its object would require getting outside our ideas, which Locke says we cannot do. The arguments Locke used to show that color is in the mind work just as well for shape. So his own principles either lead to skepticism about the material world or, as Berkeley preferred, to the conclusion that there is no such world apart from minds and their ideas. Empiricism, pushed consistently, undermined the common sense it had set out to defend.
paras.zh: 一個世代之後，柏克萊問了那個致命的問題。如果我們知覺到的永遠只是觀念，我們怎麼可能查核其中哪一個與心靈之外的東西相似？要拿一個觀念跟它的對象比較，就得走到我們的觀念之外，而洛克說我們做不到。洛克用來證明顏色在心靈之中的那些論證，用在形狀上同樣有效。所以，他自己的原則要嘛導向對物質世界的懷疑論，要嘛，如柏克萊所選擇的，導向這個結論：離開了心靈及其觀念，根本沒有這樣一個世界。經驗主義被貫徹到底，反而動搖了它原本要捍衛的常識。

problem.title_en: The philosopher of liberty and the slave trade
problem.title_zh: 自由的哲學家與奴隸貿易

paras.en: Locke’s record contains a contradiction that readers should know about. The first sentence of the Two Treatises calls slavery so vile a condition that an Englishman could hardly be imagined to plead for it. Yet Locke invested in the Royal African Company, which traded in enslaved people, and as secretary to the proprietors of the Carolina colony he had a hand in a constitution that gave every free man absolute power over his slaves. Scholars disagree about how to weigh this. Some stress that he later worked to reform colonial policy. Others hold that his theory of property was shaped to fit the colonial enterprise. Either way the case is a warning that fits the subject of this series: a person can state a principle clearly and fail to see what follows from it.
paras.zh: 洛克的生平裡有一個矛盾，讀者應該知道。《政府論兩篇》的第一句話就說，奴役是如此卑劣的處境，簡直無法想像會有英國人替它辯護。然而洛克投資了從事奴隸買賣的皇家非洲公司；而且他擔任卡羅來納殖民地業主們的秘書時，參與了一部憲法的制定，那部憲法給予每個自由人對其奴隸的絕對權力。學者對該怎麼衡量這件事意見不一。有人強調他後來致力於改革殖民政策；也有人認為，他的財產理論就是為了配合殖民事業而塑造的。不管是哪一種，這個案例都是一個警告，而且跟這個系列的主題很貼切：一個人可以把一個原則說得很清楚，卻看不見從它推得出什麼。

said.claim: Locke wrote that everyone has a right to “life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness.”
said.claim_zh: 洛克寫過，人人都有「生命、自由與追求幸福」的權利。
said.en: The phrase is Thomas Jefferson’s, from the American Declaration of Independence. Locke’s list in the Second Treatise is “life, health, liberty, or possessions,” and elsewhere “lives, liberties and estates.” Jefferson kept Locke’s structure and replaced property with happiness, a change whose meaning historians still discuss.
said.zh: 這個詞組是傑佛遜的，出自美國《獨立宣言》。洛克在《政府論下篇》裡列的是「生命、健康、自由或財物」，別處則是「生命、自由與產業」。傑佛遜保留了洛克的架構，把「財產」換成了「幸福」；這個改動的意義，歷史學家至今仍在討論。

paras.en: Locke came closer to a Buddhist position than he could have known, on the question of what a person is. Descartes had located the self in a thinking substance. Locke argued that we have no clear idea of any such substance, and that it would make no difference to me if the substance behind my thoughts were changed every day, provided my consciousness carried on. Personal identity, he concluded, consists in continuity of consciousness, above all in memory: “as far as this consciousness can be extended backwards to any past action or thought, so far reaches the identity of that person.” The self is a relation among experiences, and no underlying thing is needed.
paras.zh: 在「人是什麼」這個問題上，洛克比他自己所能知道的，更靠近佛教的立場。笛卡兒把自我安放在一個思考的實體裡。洛克論證說，我們對任何這樣的實體都沒有清楚的觀念；而且，只要我的意識延續下去，就算我思想背後的實體每天換一個，對我也沒有任何差別。他的結論是：人格同一性在於意識的連續，尤其在於記憶：「這個意識能夠向後延伸到過去的任何行為或思想有多遠，那個人的同一性就達到多遠。」自我是經驗之間的一種關係，並不需要底下有一個東西。

paras.en: A Buddhist philosopher would agree with the negative half and question the positive one. That there is no soul-substance is the doctrine of anattā. But memory seems too thin a thread: I do not stop being responsible for what I have forgotten. Buddhist accounts tie the stages of a life together by causal continuity, each moment conditioning the next, of which memory is only one strand. When Derek Parfit revived Locke’s approach in the twentieth century he widened it in exactly this way, and remarked that the Buddha would have agreed (Dharma and the West, D2).
paras.zh: 佛教哲學家會同意否定的那一半，並且質疑肯定的那一半。沒有「靈魂實體」，這正是無我的教義。但是記憶這條線似乎太細：我並不會因為忘了自己做過的事，就不必為它負責。佛教的說法是用因果的連續把一生的各個階段繫在一起：每一剎那作為下一剎那的條件；記憶只是其中的一股。二十世紀帕菲特重新啟用洛克的進路時，正是朝這個方向把它拓寬的，並且說佛陀會同意他（佛法與西方哲學 D2）。

terms.d_en: In Locke, whatever the mind is directly aware of when it perceives or thinks.
terms.d_zh: 在洛克，指心靈在知覺或思考時直接察覺到的任何東西。

terms.d_en: Qualities that objects have in themselves (shape, size, motion), and powers in objects to cause sensations in us (color, taste).
terms.d_zh: 物體本身具有的性質（形狀、大小、運動），以及物體在我們身上引起感覺的能力（顏色、味道）。

terms.d_en: The worry that if we perceive only ideas, the world behind them is hidden from us.
terms.d_zh: 這個疑慮：如果我們知覺到的只是觀念，觀念背後的世界就對我們隱而不顯。

terms.d_en: Rights that people have by nature and not by grant of any government.
terms.d_zh: 人依本性而有、並非任何政府所賜予的權利。

terms.d_en: The principle that political authority is legitimate only if those subject to it agree.
terms.d_zh: 政治權威唯有得到受其管轄者的同意才算正當，這個原則。

terms.d_en: The policy of not using the state’s power to compel religious belief.
terms.d_zh: 不動用國家權力強迫宗教信仰的政策。

quiz.q: How did Locke say his Essay began?
options: A discussion among friends stalled, and he decided to examine what the understanding can deal with.
Newton asked him to write it.
He dreamed it in exile.
It was commissioned by the king.

quiz.q: What is the difference between primary and secondary qualities?
options: Primary qualities belong to objects themselves; secondary qualities are powers to produce sensations in us.
Primary qualities are more beautiful.
Secondary qualities are learned later in life.
There is no difference.

quiz.q: What was Berkeley’s objection to Locke?
options: If we perceive only ideas, we cannot check whether they resemble anything outside the mind.
Ideas do not exist.
Experience is unnecessary for knowledge.
Locke had copied Descartes.

further.t: John Locke, An Essay Concerning Human Understanding
further.n_en: The Epistle to the Reader and Book II, chapters 1, 8, and 27.
further.n_zh: 讀〈致讀者書〉與卷二第 1、8、27 章。

further.t: John Locke, Second Treatise of Government
further.n_en: Chapters 2, 5, and 19.

philosophers.name: David Hume
philosophers.tag_en: He followed empiricism to its conclusions about cause, self, and reason, and remained the most cheerful of philosophers.
philosophers.tag_zh: 他把經驗主義一路推到它對因果、自我與理性的結論，卻始終是最開朗的哲學家。
facts: University of Edinburgh, from about age eleven
A Treatise of Human Nature (1739–40); An Enquiry Concerning Human Understanding (1748); Dialogues Concerning Natural Religion (1779)

life.h_en: A book written in his twenties

paras.en: Hume was born in Edinburgh in 1711 and grew up on his family’s small estate near the English border. His father died when he was two. He went to the University of Edinburgh at about eleven, which was early even for the time, and was expected to become a lawyer. He found that he could not bear the law and wanted only to read philosophy. At eighteen, he later said, there opened up to him “a new scene of thought,” and he worked at it so hard that his health broke down for several years.
paras.zh: 休謨 1711 年生於愛丁堡，在家族位於英格蘭邊界附近的小莊園長大。他兩歲時父親去世。大約十一歲他就進了愛丁堡大學，即使在當時也算早；家人期待他當律師。他發現自己受不了法律，只想讀哲學。他後來說，十八歲那年，「一片新的思想景象」在他面前展開；他用功到健康崩潰了好幾年。

paras.en: In 1734 he went to France to live cheaply and write, and settled at La Flèche, the town where Descartes had gone to school. There, between the ages of twenty-three and twenty-six, he wrote A Treatise of Human Nature. It is one of the great books of philosophy, and it failed. “It fell dead-born from the press,” he wrote, without even exciting a murmur among the zealots. He concluded that the fault lay in the manner and not the matter, and spent years recasting its arguments in shorter and more graceful works.
paras.zh: 1734 年他前往法國，為的是省錢過日子、專心寫作；他落腳在拉弗萊什，就是笛卡兒求學的那個小鎮。在那裡，從二十三歲到二十六歲，他寫了《人性論》。這是哲學史上的偉大著作之一，而它失敗了。他寫道：「它一出印刷廠就是個死胎」，連在狂熱分子當中激起一聲低語都沒有。他斷定毛病出在寫法、不在內容，於是花了多年，把書裡的論證改寫成比較短、比較優雅的作品。

paras.en: Hume never held a university post. He applied for the chair of moral philosophy at Edinburgh in 1745 and for a chair at Glasgow a few years later, and both times the clergy blocked him on the ground that he was an unbeliever. He earned his living as tutor to a mad nobleman, as secretary to a general, and then as keeper of the Advocates’ Library in Edinburgh, which gave him the books he needed to write a six-volume History of England. The History made him rich and, in his own time, far more famous than his philosophy did.
paras.zh: 休謨從來沒有擔任過大學教職。1745 年他申請愛丁堡大學的道德哲學教席，幾年後又申請格拉斯哥大學的一個教席；兩次都被神職人員擋下，理由是他不信神。他靠當一位瘋癲貴族的家庭教師、當一位將軍的秘書謀生，後來擔任愛丁堡律師公會圖書館的館長；這個職位給了他寫六卷本《英國史》所需要的書。《英國史》讓他致富，而且在他自己的時代，帶給他的名聲遠遠超過他的哲學。

paras.en: In 1763 he went to Paris as secretary to the British ambassador and found himself a celebrity. The French called him le bon David, and he was by every account a kind, sociable, and very fat man who loved good dinners. He tried to help the persecuted Jean-Jacques Rousseau by bringing him to England, and Rousseau, growing suspicious, accused him of plotting against him. The quarrel entertained Europe.
paras.zh: 1763 年他以英國大使秘書的身分前往巴黎，發現自己成了名人。法國人叫他「好人大衛」（le bon David）；從各方面的記載看，他是個和善、好交際、非常胖、喜歡美食的人。他試著幫助受迫害的盧梭，把他帶到英國；而盧梭疑心日重，反過來指控他密謀陷害自己。這場爭吵成了全歐洲的談資。

paras.en: He retired to Edinburgh, where he cooked for his friends and revised his works. In 1775 he learned that he had a fatal disorder of the bowels. He faced death without fear and without changing his views, to the dismay of James Boswell, who visited to see whether an unbeliever could really die calmly. He arranged for his Dialogues Concerning Natural Religion, which he had kept unpublished for twenty-five years, to appear after his death. His friend Adam Smith wrote that he had always considered him “as approaching as nearly to the idea of a perfectly wise and virtuous man, as perhaps the nature of human frailty will permit.”
paras.zh: 他退休回到愛丁堡，在那裡為朋友下廚，並且修訂自己的著作。1775 年他得知自己患了致命的腸疾。他面對死亡毫無恐懼，也沒有改變看法；這讓詹姆斯・包斯威爾很沮喪，包斯威爾特地去探望，想看看一個不信神的人是不是真的能平靜地死去。他安排好，讓那部他壓了二十五年沒有發表的《自然宗教對話錄》在他死後問世。他的朋友亞當・斯密寫道，自己向來認為他「接近一個完美的智者與有德者的理想，接近到人類脆弱的本性或許容許的極限」。

timeline: History of England begins to appear

idea.title_en: The central idea: Every idea is a copy of an impression
idea.title_zh: 核心觀念：每個觀念都是印象的摹本

paras.en: Hume divides the contents of the mind into impressions, which are the vivid perceptions we have when we see, feel, love, or hate, and ideas, which are the faint copies of these that we use in thinking. His first principle is that every simple idea is copied from an earlier impression. This gives him a test. When a philosopher uses a word, ask from what impression the supposed idea is derived. If none can be found, the word has no meaning.
paras.zh: 休謨把心靈的內容分成「印象」與「觀念」：印象是我們在看、感受、愛、恨的時候所擁有的鮮明知覺；觀念是這些印象的微弱摹本，我們用它們來思考。他的第一原則是：每一個簡單觀念，都是從先前的某個印象摹寫來的。這給了他一個檢驗。當一位哲學家使用一個詞，就問：這個所謂的觀念，是從哪一個印象來的？如果一個都找不到，這個詞就沒有意義。

paras.en: He then applies the test to the most important ideas in philosophy, with destructive results. Necessary connection: we have an impression of one event following another and none of any tie between them. The self: “when I enter most intimately into what I call myself, I always stumble on some particular perception or other,” and so a person is “nothing but a bundle or collection of different perceptions.” Moral judgment: no observation of an act reveals its wrongness, which lies in the feeling of the observer, and no statement of what ought to be can be deduced from statements of what is. Even action is ruled by feeling: “Reason is, and ought only to be the slave of the passions.” Reason can tell us how to get what we want. It cannot tell us what to want.
paras.zh: 接著他把這個檢驗用在哲學裡最重要的幾個觀念上，結果是毀滅性的。必然連結：我們有「一個事件跟在另一個之後」的印象，卻沒有它們之間任何紐帶的印象。自我：「當我最貼近地進入我稱為『自己』的東西時，我總是碰到某個個別的知覺」，所以一個人「不過是一束或一堆不同的知覺」。道德判斷：對一個行為再怎麼觀察，也看不到它的「錯」；錯在觀察者的感受裡；而任何關於「應該如何」的陳述，都無法從關於「是如何」的陳述演繹出來。連行動也由感受統治：「理性是、而且只應該是激情的奴隸。」理性能告訴我們怎樣得到想要的東西；它不能告訴我們該想要什麼。

quote.en: Be a philosopher; but, amidst all your philosophy, be still a man.
quote.zh: 做一個哲學家吧；但是，在你一切的哲學當中，仍然要做一個人。
quote.ref: Hume, An Enquiry Concerning Human Understanding, section I
quote.note_en: Nature’s advice to the thinker, as Hume imagines it, and a fair summary of how he lived.
quote.note_zh: 休謨想像中「自然」給思想者的忠告，也相當貼切地概括了他自己的活法。

objection.title_en: The strongest objection: His own fork cuts him
objection.title_zh: 最強的反駁：他自己的叉子刺到了他

paras.en: The Enquiry ends with one of the most quoted paragraphs in philosophy. Take any book, Hume says, and ask whether it contains abstract reasoning about quantity or number, or experimental reasoning about matters of fact. If it contains neither, “Commit it then to the flames: for it can contain nothing but sophistry and illusion.” The obvious question is which of the two the Enquiry itself contains. The claim that all meaningful statements fall into these two classes is not a truth of mathematics. It does not look like a report of experiments either. By its own test the book seems to belong in the fire. The same difficulty returned in the twentieth century for the logical positivists, who revived Hume’s principle and were asked how it could itself be verified.
paras.zh: 《人類理解研究》的結尾，是哲學裡被引用最多的段落之一。休謨說，隨便拿起一本書，問它是否包含關於量或數的抽象推理，或者關於實際事情的實驗推理。如果兩者都沒有，「那就把它投進火裡：因為它包含的只能是詭辯與幻象。」顯而易見的問題是：《人類理解研究》本身包含的是這兩者中的哪一種？「一切有意義的陳述都落在這兩類之中」這個主張，並不是數學真理；看起來也不像實驗報告。照它自己的檢驗，這本書似乎該進火堆。同樣的困難在二十世紀又回到邏輯實證論者身上：他們重新啟用休謨的原則，然後被人問到，這個原則本身要怎麼檢證。

paras.en: Kant’s objection goes deeper. Hume assumed that the mind receives impressions passively and that order must be found among them. Kant replied that a stream of unconnected impressions would not be an experience of anything. To perceive a ball moving, one must already connect what is seen now with what was seen a moment ago, according to rules. The connections Hume could not find in his impressions are, on this view, what the mind contributes in order to have experience at all. Kant said it was Hume who “first interrupted my dogmatic slumber.”
paras.zh: 康德的反駁更深。休謨假定，心靈是被動地接受印象的，而秩序必須在印象當中去找。康德回答說，一連串互不相連的印象，根本算不上對任何東西的經驗。要知覺到一顆球在動，人必須已經按照規則，把此刻看見的跟片刻之前看見的連結起來。休謨在印象裡找不到的那些連結，照這個看法，正是心靈為了能有經驗而貢獻的東西。康德說，是休謨「首先打斷了我獨斷的沉睡」。

problem.title_en: A footnote that has not been forgiven
problem.title_zh: 一條沒有被原諒的註腳

paras.en: Hume’s reputation for good sense and good nature makes one passage harder to read. In a footnote added in 1753 to his essay “Of National Characters,” he wrote that he was inclined to suspect that Black people were naturally inferior to whites, and he dismissed a report of a learned Black man in Jamaica as probably exaggerated. The claim had no basis in evidence and was challenged in his own day by the philosopher James Beattie, among others. He revised the note late in life and did not withdraw it. In 2020 the University of Edinburgh removed his name from one of its buildings. The passage is sometimes excused as a prejudice of the age. It is fairer to say that the philosopher who told us to proportion belief to evidence failed, on this subject, to do so, and that the failure did harm.
paras.zh: 休謨以明理與好脾氣著稱，這讓有一段文字更難讀下去。1753 年，他在〈論民族性〉這篇文章加了一條註腳，寫道他傾向於懷疑黑人天生不如白人，並且把關於牙買加一位有學問的黑人的報導，當作多半言過其實而不予理會。這個主張沒有任何證據基礎，在他自己的時代就受到哲學家貝蒂等人的質疑。他晚年修改過這條註腳，但沒有撤回。2020 年，愛丁堡大學把他的名字從校內一棟建築上拿掉。這段文字有時被當成「時代的偏見」而獲得開脫。比較公允的說法是：這位教我們「使信念與證據成比例」的哲學家，在這個題目上沒有做到，而這個失誤造成了傷害。

said.en: His contemporaries called him “the great infidel,” and his arguments against miracles, the design argument, and the immortality of the soul are devastating. But he never described himself as an atheist, and his Dialogues end without a verdict. A story from Paris, told by Diderot, has him remark at dinner that he had never seen an atheist, and his host reply that he was sitting at table with seventeen. On his own principles, to assert that there is no God would go beyond the evidence as surely as asserting that there is one.
said.zh: 他同時代的人稱他為「大異教徒」；他反對神蹟、反對設計論證、反對靈魂不朽的論證，都是毀滅性的。但他從來沒有自稱無神論者，他的《對話錄》結尾也沒有下判決。有一個出自巴黎、由狄德羅轉述的故事：他在晚宴上說自己從沒見過無神論者，主人回答說，同桌就坐著十七位。照他自己的原則，斷言「沒有上帝」，跟斷言「有上帝」一樣，都確確實實超出了證據。

paras.en: No Western philosopher sounds more Buddhist than Hume on the self. He looked inward for the owner of his experiences and found only the experiences, “a bundle or collection of different perceptions, which succeed each other with an inconceivable rapidity, and are in a perpetual flux and movement.” A Theravāda monk analyzing the person into five aggregates would say almost the same. The psychologist Alison Gopnik has even argued that Hume could have heard of Buddhist ideas at La Flèche, where one of the Jesuits had lived in Siam and knew a fellow missionary’s report on Tibetan Buddhism. The evidence is circumstantial, and most scholars think Hume reached his view independently.
paras.zh: 在自我這個問題上，沒有哪一位西方哲學家聽起來比休謨更像佛教徒。他往內找自己種種經驗的主人，找到的只有經驗：「一束或一堆不同的知覺，以不可思議的速度彼此相續，處於永恆的流變與運動之中。」一位把人分析為五蘊的上座部比丘，說的幾乎是同樣的話。心理學家艾莉森・高普尼克甚至論證過，休謨有可能在拉弗萊什聽說過佛教的觀念：那裡有一位耶穌會士曾經住過暹羅，並且知道一位傳教士同伴關於藏傳佛教的報告。這些證據都是旁證，多數學者認為休謨是獨立得出這個看法的。

paras.en: The contrast lies in what each did next. Hume found his conclusions disturbing, and his remedy was to leave the study: “I dine, I play a game of backgammon, I converse, and am merry with my friends,” after which his speculations seemed cold and strained. For him the discovery that there is no self was a theoretical result with no practical use. For the Buddha it was the most practical discovery possible, because clinging to a self is the cause of suffering, and seeing through it, steadily and in experience, is release. Hume reached the insight by argument and then set it aside at dinner. The Buddhist path is a method for keeping it in view (Dharma and the West, D2).
paras.zh: 對比在於兩人接下來做了什麼。休謨覺得自己的結論令人不安，而他的解藥是離開書房：「我吃飯，我下一盤雙陸棋，我談天，跟朋友們同樂」；在那之後，他那些玄想就顯得冰冷而牽強。對他來說，「沒有自我」這個發現是一個理論上的結果，沒有實際用處。對佛陀來說，那是最實際不過的發現，因為執取一個自我正是苦的原因，而穩定地、在經驗中看穿它，就是解脫。休謨靠論證到達了這個洞見，然後在餐桌上把它擱下。佛教的道，是一套讓它一直留在視野裡的方法（佛法與西方哲學 D2）。

terms.d_en: Vivid original perceptions, and their fainter copies in thought.
terms.d_zh: 鮮明的原初知覺，以及它們在思想中較微弱的摹本。

terms.d_en: Every simple idea derives from a corresponding earlier impression.
terms.d_zh: 每一個簡單觀念，都來自一個對應的、先前的印象。

terms.d_en: The division of all knowable truths into relations of ideas and matters of fact.
terms.d_zh: 把一切可知的真理分成「觀念的關係」與「實際的事情」。

terms.d_en: The view that a person is a collection of perceptions with no underlying self.
terms.d_zh: 主張人是一堆知覺的集合，底下沒有自我。

terms.d_en: No conclusion about what ought to be follows from premises only about what is.
terms.d_zh: 從只談「是如何」的前提，推不出關於「應該如何」的結論。

terms.d_en: Hume’s own position: doubt about foundations, joined to modest reliance on experience in practice.
terms.d_zh: 休謨自己的立場：對基礎存疑，同時在實踐上適度地倚賴經驗。

quiz.q: What does Hume’s copy principle say?
options: Every simple idea is derived from an earlier impression.
Every book should be copied before it is burned.
The mind copies ideas from other minds.
Impressions are copies of ideas.

quiz.q: What did Hume find when he looked for the self?
options: Only particular perceptions, never a self apart from them.
A simple, unchanging substance.
His brain.
Nothing at all, not even perceptions.

quiz.q: Why does the last paragraph of the Enquiry seem to undermine the book?
options: The book’s own principle is neither mathematics nor experimental reasoning.
It contradicts the Treatise.
It was added by another author.
It praises metaphysics.
